If RE Revelations was released right after RE 4, then this game might have been heavily criticized for its lack of depth in the storytelling department. For a game that supposingly touches on the early days of the BSAA, I wished the game developers had put in more effort in telling the backstories of the main characters we get to play as.
Parker comes off as someone who tries too hard to impress others, while Jessica's lines were simply.....unintelligent. I thought Quint and Keith were interesting characters  but their segment was too limited. The least Capcom could do was to give an explanation as to why or how Chris and Jill had joined to BSAA, since they were the most well known characters.
Nevertheless, certain elements of your typical survivor horror game are delivered in this installment. The game may look tame on the casual and normal difficulties but start the game on the infernal mode and you may just start to hate this game.
In conclusion, Revelations is a much better alternative if you are sick of RE 6's over-the-top plotline and gameplay.  The relatively simplistic game mechanic in Revelations brings out the horror that many gamers experienced from the earlier installments.  Still, don't expect too much of a reward once you finish the game.

As a fan of hack & slash, arcade style games, I cannot justify this game's development. I love Streets of Rage, Golden Axe, Castle Crashers, Final Fight, the Konami X-Men and Simpsons games, and the arcade D&D games, but Sacred: Citadel fails in almost every way. What's more is it fails at even being a game that you want to ackowledge in the Sacred game universe. If you're a fan of Sacred 1 or 2, chances are, you will not have a good time here. Even if you play with friends, even if you like arcade games, even if you like humor about flatulence and overweight people, you will likely find this game to just be annoying. I like the occassional joke of bodily functions, but it seems like this game has more fart jokes than actual story. This game lacks style, substance, and almost any familiar tones to the games that made Sacred a great series. I like the art style, I like the animations, but everything else just annoys me. I know it's not the gameplay because if I shut my brain off, I can enjoy myself; but then a character speaks and I want to quit to desktop.
Instead of playing this, just play more Sacred 2 or Sacred 1. If you don't own those games, but you're looking at Sacred: Citadel, think again and just do yourself a favor: Buy either of the amazing, top-down, hardcore role-playing games with the right balance of humor, action, story, and character progression.

Most of what I could say has long since been said. Mostly I never feel embarrassed to give negative reviews if I feel screwed over. I figured I should also give the thumbs up to games that deserve it. And imho this game does deserve it. I have enjoyed this tyoe of game ever since the very first PanzerGeneral came out in the 90s. And OoB is a nice continuation of such games, with a few new twists that now you actually need to be careful with your supply line. I got caught a few times making "opportunity attacks" with a fast tank, as I was used to from Panzer General and Panzer Corps only to find I suddenly had the unit stuck behind enemy lines, out of supply and unable to reinforce it. Well I learned. And I enjoy. I have since played through the Morning Sun DLC since I wanted a change from always playingin the European theatre of WWII.
As far as I'm concerned, if you were a fan of the Panzer General titles and/or the newer versions Panzer Corps you should also love this game, it is very much like it's predecessors with a little extra. Ifyou are used to playing such games you can also jump right in without the tutorial, the new features are easy enough to figure out (even if you may have an emergency trying to bust your tanks out of the trap you yourself put them in LOL).
As for some of the negative reviews I had seen, with some of them I have to say "d'uh". Yes it is true that if you are a WWII game veteran, the battles you fight are very familiar... That's because these are HISTORIC battles. They won't change the history of WWII just because you get bored playing the same battles over again.
No, (so far?) in the Pacific theater of the war you cannot play the Chinese. Maybe they will add it later, maybe not. But I have had a blast playing the Japanese in the war against China and I'm looking forward to importing my core units into the battle against the US which I will start as soon as I'm done praising the game.
Anyway, I have bought all of the DLC out so far and I'm looking forward to many more hours of play time, playing them through one by one.

The vanilla version is great, but just like all Total War games the mods really make this one of the best strategy games.
Quick highlight: Real time battles mixed with a turn based campaign, you control a country and their ruling family with the goal of building armies and conquering your neighbor countries. The map covers most of Europe with North Africa and the Middle East.
Pros: Battles are very satisfying when you win, timeplan spans hundreds of years, you can follow the members of your royal family as they are born, achieve great victories, and die. There are a lot of mods that greatly enhance the game.
Cons: Very little depth, there isn't much to getting a robust economy other than growing in size; there is very little political intrigue inside your own family (ala Game of Thrones style); and armies can be over simplified. There are only twenty two countries, and the game is called Total War for a reason: allies do not exist.
Overall great game, give it a try if you're looking for a game where you can rewrite history.

Not likely to change anyone's decision, but I'll mention this is my first review. I did not expect what I found at all. This game is too well done to let it fail; so I will do what I can to promote it.
This review was written as of  build 0.7.1. Game/story only goes up to, not including, the second dungeon.
TL:DR
Pros:
- Well drawn/animated
- Challenging combat and puzzle sections.
- Relatable realistic character interation.
Cons:
- At build 0.7.1, there isn't a whole lot of story yet. It took up 12 hours at this point with minimal side-questing, so I won't say it's short, just incomplete.
- A bit grind heavy when getting items to trade with. There are some traders that trade for the basics, but it still requires some other items to get them. More common items, but still. Keep in mind you don't have to trade. You can find equipment in the wild if you search the areas at more than a simple glance.
Full Opinion:
Downloaded the demo first to have a look. It seemed like a decent retro-style action/adventure that might be fun for a few hours. I was utterly blown away by what I found. The tutorial is a short 10 minutes or so explanation to just give the most basic parts. The combat is fairly simple, but the abilities you learn are well done and fun to use. The enemies are implemented in a way that you will have a hard time if you just run around hitting the attack button. Personally I always feel most games are a little too easy these days, so that's a plus to me. The puzzles are varied, sufficiently chanllenging, and introduce new ideas without burying you in tutorial. The new ideas are added without warning or explanation. You'll just walk into a room, see a switch or button you need, and ask yourself "How do I get that? Maybe I should try this new object over here? But how does it work? Hit it? Shoot it? Fire? Slide on the ice?" As for the story, there hasn't been much developement at this point. There are two main plots. The plot for the MMO is a generic "gather the elements" type of quest, but they have handled it well so far (more or less paying homage to how MMO's often are and how players would act toward them) and have spoken of a far deeper narrative beneath it. The plot outside of the MMO (How the herione got there and why) hasn't moved much just yet. Personally, I find the character interaction to be a shining example of how to flesh out character traits without over-playing it. You don't need slapstick gags or some running joke to make them memorable. Between that and the well drawn character portraits for these sections, the story segments are honestly a joy.
Great graphics, but the controls leave something to be desired and the amount of grinding required takes any of the fun away.

The Binding of Isaac was recommended to me by a friend for no reason other than he liked it. And so, I purchased it and spent a good amount of time playing through it. There are some really great things about it and some very small not so great things that are fortunately outweighed by the great things.
The replayability of this game is fantastic. There are a lot of random acheivements to get and because the game is randomly generated each time, it's never the same twice.
You feel really awesome about yourself when you do really really well in a run through, even if it's just getting a hair further than your last run.
The controls are odd at first, but you get the hang of them soon enough and it's really easy to grasp them within a few mintutes.
The bad stuff of the game, I feel, is just how incredibly hard it can be. Sometimes it feels like the game is just so unfair at points for no reason at all. Again, because of the random generation, sometimes you will get really good items and easy rooms to beat, and sometimes your combination with be terrible items with really hard rooms to beat. It makes one in every ten runs incredibly frustrating.
All that said, it's a great game, and it's nice to play if you have fifteen minutes or fifteen hours to kill.

It's hard to objectively define Deadly Premonition. Perhaps it's a game so bad that it's somehow good. Perhaps it's a game intentionally bizarre and profound which is rough around the edges. Either way, it's not a forgettable game. That much is certain.
If I tried to review it on it's merits, the review would come across overly negative - the simple reason being it lacks them. Graphically it's poor. The soundtrack is forgettable. The gameplay is fairly boring. The controls are pretty bad. The constant onslaught of driving from place to place is dull. I could go on.
Despite this, the plot while hardly a masterpiece is just weird enough to keep you hooked. The protagonist is curiously unusual and his supporting cast unpredictable. All things considered, the game rarely goes where you expect it to, breaking most of it's tropes and keeping things fresh. It's suffice to say you'll keep playing just to see what crazy sh*t Deadly Premonition pulls next.
That is, if you can make it work. The PC port is nothing short of awful. In order to get a smooth experience, you'll need mods. At minimum, DPFix should be used. For a more solid, enjoyable experience, you can use some texture mods and SweetFX. The game is also full of bugs. I had to launch the game from the main exe as the launcher was incapable of doing so. I also had to patch the game to be large-address aware due to a fairly aggressive memory leak. I'd also strongly recommend a gamepad. Even after all this, the game still has a number of issues, but it's certainly playable.
So, do I recommend Deadly Premonition? I'd say yes, but barely. Pick it up cheap and hope to heck you can make it work. If so, you're in for a wild ride... for better or for worse.

After playing this game for 900+ hours, I think it is safe to say I know what I am talking about when I give the revuew for this NBA2K Installment.
First and foremost, to not waste anybody's time. iF THERE IS ANY NEWER NBA2K GAME THAT IS RELEASED AND YOU THINK OF BUYING AN OLDER VERSION, DO NOT. CHANCES ARE THE NEWER VERSIONS ARE BETTER.
Ok, with that said, lets get on with the review. As a casual player, the MyCareer mode is usually the first mode I choose the play, and let me tell you, compared to the previous game? This year's MyCareer feels SO SO deep. (♥♥♥♥ Spike Lee and his stupid NBA2K18 MyCareer Story that kept me occupied for only like 2 hours even though I love the Knicks) The timetables in a day are split up more evenly to giv e a better variety of how you want to spend the day progressing your character whichbrings a more diverse approach to the game. However, like every NBA2K MyCareer, it still eventually feels very grindy and repetitive and you might get bored of it (Even though the Orange Juice function is sick and all)
You know how you see advertisements in Mcdonalds of a Big Mac and it looks like the tastiest♥♥♥♥♥♥in the world but then when you actually go down to a McDonalds and buy one and it is presented in a clumsy manner that looks nothing at all like advertised and that makes you feel sad and cheated on the inside? That is how I will describe the MyGM and MyLeague features of the game.

A straight-up upscaled port of a 3-year-old 3DS game, which retails for $20, sold for $50.
The campaign is short, the levels are extremely cramped and linear, and load times (though hidden) are frequent, as befitting the original hardware for which they were designed.
All that being said, if you can catch it for the price of the 3DS version or less, it's a far better Resident Evil game than Capcom's latest fiascos, keeping more in line with the gameplay style of RE5, and making an attempt to return to spookiness and atmosphere over explosions and bolo ties. There are even tense underwater sections, and the return of the master of unlocking!
The cherry on top is raid mode, an online cooperative mode for two players, where you fight your way through snippets of the campaign, albeit with more aggressive enemy placement. You collect loot, unlock characters and costumes, and attempt to score well to earn points for purchasing and upgrading skills and equipment. It ties into Capcom's bizarre
website, as well, so you can get a little more use out of the damn thing if you made one for RE6.
Overall, a pretty great game, and something of a return to form for the Resident Evil series.

Having grown up with the earlier Resident Evils and suffering through the mess that was Resident Evil 5, I had little hope that Capcom could recover from the damage they've done to the franchise. But, hey, they thankfully proved me wrong with a game that was originally a 3DS spin off. With Revelations, the series once again gains survival horror like settings, atmosphere, and mechanics while still maintaining all the improvements made with the controls.
For the older fans: You'll get a decent amount of survival horror atmosphere, along with the ammo conservation mechanics. It's nowhere near the golden days of Resident Evil 1-CV but it's leagues above the stuff they pulled with Resident Evil 5. Heck, it's a start in the right direction right? The story as well actually feels like a throwback to the earlier games with a lot of chess moves going on in the background and you the player trying to figure out the mystery before the game reveals it. Of course most importantly, they brought the item chest back. I only serves to hold extra fire arms in this game but having inventory management in a RE game after such a long time, was a nice surprise.
For the newer fans: All the great things about Resident Evil 4's controls are still there, ammo isn't limited enough that you can't go on a small shooting spree on normal or lower difficulty, and action sequences are sprinkled through the entire game. So if you like the action side more of the franchise, you can have fun with Revelations with the understanding it's not 4 or 5 in terms of shooting everything that comes at you.
To wrap this up, this is a great game compared to the junk Capcom has released in the RE franchise these couple of years. Good story, exploration, running from enemies, good narrative, and interesting enemy designs(though they get repetitive after a while.) I hope Capcom lets the team behind this game continue to do their own thing of bringing back the series closer to its original form because fans will response to that with purchases. Meanwhile, Capcom can use the main series to continue to try and force a square peg in a round hole with their "No, no, it's not a rip-off of Call of Duty. It's action survival, trust us." With the magic that was Resident Evil 6, I'm sure that's working beautifully for them.

Resident Evil Revelations is, for Resident Evil standards, and considering in which direction Resident Evil 4 and Resident Evil 5 were going, a really good game, No kidding. To be fair, I liked Resident Evil 4 & 5 regardless. But Revelations makes a lot better than its predecessors.
On the positive side we have a lot of helpful features keeping the game fresh and making it stand out. You can now move while aiming and shooting, effectively increasing mobility and, above all else, fun. Seriously, how many times did we get annoyed by the "You are aiming and can not move" mechanic of the other games? Right, a lot. Also, your knife now functions by pressing the attack key without aiming providing quicker access to melee combat. It's still not spectacular or even helpful to fight with the knife and you're basically screwed if you have to resort to do so, but hey.
Then there's your health bar.
Remember how you got a single full health bar in RE 5 and no separate compartments, rendering any herb that wasn't combined with another useless? Well, they got completely rid of that by giving you no health bar at all but instead take a sort of CoD approach by having blood around the screen, indicating your life. If the screen becomes less colour saturated and there's a lot of blood on the edges of your screen, you better get healed.
Also, the healing system is more convenient. You now cancarry a set amount of herbs with you at any given time and you completely heal with a single herb upon the press of a single button, making it harder to waste herbs. Or easier, depending on you and how trigger-happy you are.
Staying with "can carry a set amount of X", you can only carry so much ammo of one type with you. You can increase your maximum ammo capacity by collecting ammo pouches but as for your inventory, no space is stolen by ammo you don't need. You just collect ammo or any items for that matter of one type until you can not carry any more of this item, while all the other items still have room.
Your inventory has been reworked, too. But I guess I just explained everything you need to know.
As for the story itself, it isn't all that bad actually. Well, it's a side story that surprisingly has nothing to do with Wesker whatsoever, but hey, it works. Huh. What else? Well, the graphics are better, there aren't any emblems to e collected anymore and instead of a classic merc mode you got the raid mode. Running through an obstacle course of enemies and trying to reach the end. Also, the raid mode now is the place where you unlock costumes for your characters in both campaign mode and raid mode.
And last but not least: The horror's back! Well, at least a little. The game is dark, almost all of the time, the music in the background plays its role well, too. And some of the boss fights, especially the first real boss fight, gives you the feeling of "Oh my GOD goawaygoawaygoaway". Finally, some ray of hope for the series.
But there are also some serious downsides to the game.
The dodging mechanic is just horrendously complicated to execute. You dodge with either your space key (which is quick turn) or your W key (which is moving forward), making it nigh impossible to time your dodges correctly and you almost always end up getting hit. At other times, you just dodge at random without you even lifting a finger. Seriously, this is one screwed-up mechanic. I never actively tried to dodge because of that. Played through the game regardless.
The cutscenes have gotten worse for some reason. And I dunno how they screwed this up. I mean... it worked well in RE 5, why doesn't it work well in RER, too?
And then there's the setting. The usual RE game takes place in one country and you travel to various locations within their boundaries to kill the end boss. In RER, the game takes place on a ship. One. Single. Ship. Can you imagine just how boring that setting can get? The first few hours of the game involve a LOT of backtracking and if you don't have a lot of patience you end up quitting the game and say "F*** it".
Luckily, the ship is a big♥♥♥♥♥luxury liner with a lot of different-looking parts, like a huge dining hall, engine rooms, a pool... but overall it's the same ship. Some missions involve you going aboard another ship! :D ...only to then find out it's an exact copy of the ship you saw before. No, seriously, it even says so in the story.
Well, the setting isn't all THAT bad tbh. I mean, there's the different areas of the ship(s). And then there are some playable flashbacks or playable missions carried out by other characters that take place simultaneously which are in completely different areas. You will see a big ship, a beach, snowy mountains and a lot of infested crap.
The enemies.
Well, they are creative, I give 'em that. They are all sea-based so expect a lot of fishy things going on. As for classic zombies, you won't find any of them in this game. A lot of fish-human merged mutants comes your way instead. It's a nice thing but I was kinda weirded out the first couple of minutes.
But I have to say the story of that game seems kinda insignificant to me. It doesn't involve Umbrella in any way, there are no zombies (so to speak) and there is no Albert Wesker. It just doesn't seem like a major event, although the threat you are combating and considering what's at stake (if we are thinking about the BSAA for a minute) is pretty serious. But somehow it doesn't really convey that urgency we know from other titles. Perhaps they shouldn't have put in the major character cast of Chris Redfield and Jill Valentine.
Speaking of which, the amount of totally new characters is huge. So many new faces. Funny faces. By that I mean the game's got a lot of cheesy humour. I adore that, lightens up the experience and, if you switch on the Japanese voiceover, you'll feel like being in an anime. Also it was nice to see some fresh characters. I like the old ones, don't get me wrong, but something new is always a good idea. Well. Almost. *cough* Las Plagas *cough* (I didn't like the Las Plagas).
Anyway...
I gotta say: the game's pretty good! It's got some of its mojo back imo. And it has a lot of neat little features that make the game better than RE 4 & 5. If you liked RE 5, I recommend playing RER. It's a good game.

Not reinventing the wheel in any regard (everything in it has been seen somewhere else before, including the gun customization), but decently looking with a coherent style, quickly started and smoothly running. Mostly standard game modes (CTF, TDM, KotH and something combining them called "Annihilation"). Fun if you go don't care too much about balance aspects, or if you have friends to run with. Otherwise you will likely find a lot of rage in this game. The teams are so small and the gunplay depends enough on twitching reflexes and "imba" loadouts that you will lose a lot if you run with random newbies against skilled and stacked parties. The sheer skill of one player alone can already decide a match before it has really started. The in- and endgame-taunting and the general CoD-likeliness with it's completely randomized matchmaking system - you can never know nor decide where and with who to play unless you form parties - will increase the hate and whining the community of this game will surely generate. I've seen this happen in other similar games plenty of times. Enough reason for me to stay away from it. I prefer other kinds of shooters - less rage-induced and noobie-stomping ones.

This game is plainly just good. As most shooters in the modern era go for the most part its either a COD copy or COD. On top of that balancing is a joke with the new leveling systems most of those games have now instituted.
Loadout takes balancing to a whole new level. It puts everyone on equal footing and my proof you ask? Well I suck at ALL shooters, but just recently I got a triple kill on an opposing team that was clearly wiping the floor with not only me but my whole team. It's about skill, about choices YOU make.
The best part is that everything is COMPLETELY tailored to your playstyle. And that is brought in with the weaponcrafting system. You want to sniper? Then you make that rifle exactly how you want it... rocketmonkey? Build the perfect rocket launcher. As a whole if more shooters had that kind of freedom it would improve balance, not make it worse as is believed.
It must be said that the general aesthetic is NOT for kids. That being said, HOLY CRAP is it funny. The over the top visual style and extremely gory deaths means even when you're dying you're having fun. The way damage is shown on your character is AMAZING to say the least.
My final thoughts: This is FREE TO PLAY!!!! This is not free to pay or pay to win as many "Free" games are. Plus this is basically an Indie title, and they have done a lot of things right here that AAA Publishers fail to even concieve of. There are places in which they can clearly improve, such as the matchmaking and inviting of friends to games, but nothing is perfect. As long as fun is had then it's good.

A bad port of an already creaky game, the first enemy you will face in this game is the game itself.  Google DPfix - the patch made by a saintly individual who also rescued the Dark Souls port - as this is essential.  The controls will annoy you, the generally clunkiness will annoy you, and the combat will definitely annoy you.
But here's the thing:  I'm recommending it, and rather forcefully.  From a technical standpoint it's terrible, and don't get me wrong, it's shocking, but the actual content of the game acts as a huge counterweight.  You'll get over the annoyances and get sucked in to this little town, in which you can get up to what you're supposed to be up to as an FBI agent, or simply dawdle, have lunch at the diner, go fishing, then get hammered a bar in the evening.  You spend your time in this town however you choose to, and although the main plot is always there, waiting to progress and conclude, there's always time to just enjoy the town.  This is one of the few games in which you, as an agent of the law, can make the active choice to just have a day off - and that doesn't mean just pausing proceedings, it means potentially finding interesting side-stories as you take it easy.
For all that it lacks in the technical department, it does something that the Elder Scrolls games are vocal about doing but have yet to actually achieve:  a convincing town, with people acting as individuals with their own priorities and schedules.  I can't think of another game in which this has been achieved quite so well.

There's a reason why survival horror is so distinct from other shooters : you don't want to fight. If you fight, its because you got backed in a corner, that you have no other choice. Megabyte Punch is a great platform brawler game you should be playing, but you'd better no come into it expecting to play Smash Bros.
For one, the movement options are fairly limited. Sideways movement uses digital input regardless of whether you're using a keyboard or a gamepad, making small position tweaks nearly impossible; you also have to double-tap a direction to dash, which makes the action clunkier and gives it some considerable human-based delay. You're also allowed to block while in the air, but there's no action that to controls your falling speed, making air combat more predictable as a result.
The collectable parts are really fun, even if it means you've got to rely on random drops. Some parts share the same moves, both in the same part slot and in different ones, allowing you to build a robot with whichever version's more useful to you, or with whatever looks cooler. My only gripe with the parts is how projectiles-firing ones are really scarce, have only a few movement patterns (except for the regular blaster), and most of them can be easily deflected by blocking at the right time, which isn't hard at all.
Allowing multiple players to play in adventure mode was a great idea, but not allowing AI-controlled opponents in the versus mode means you'll be needing three or four players for versus matches to be fun.

In short: This game is amazing, and you should be buying it right now. Even it's in incomplete state, it's a masterpiece.
Detailed review:
Graphics 10/10 - CrossCode has a beautiful 16-bit art style. This really comes to shine in the gorgeous close-up portraits of the characters seen during dialogues. Not only that, the world is also amazingly beautiful with small details everywhere that really make you think the devs care deeply about the looks of their game. If I only cared about the visuals, then those alone would've made me buy the game.
Music 9/10 - Not a lot to say here, the music is just all around nice. And there's a lot of unique pieces heard in different areas of the game.
Combat 10/10 - Combat in this game feels really fluid and every hit feels impactful. There are many ways to utilize your base kit - throwing balls, fighting melee, guarding, and dashing - and your talent trees and equipment offer a lot of customization. On top of that, there are 4 elemental attack modes.
Puzzles 10/10 - Probably my favourite part of this game. The puzzle design in CrossCode is just genius. Never did the puzzles feel unfairly hard or frustrating, but they always offered a fair bit of challenge. Currently, there are 4 proper dungeons that combine puzzles and combat together. Some enemies are puzzles themselves - you need to figure out a way to beat them, just going in and fisting everybody is not the solution. Key parts of the puzzles are the ball throwing mechanic and different elemental interactions.
Story 10/10 - The story is probably my second-favourite thing about CrossCode, although it's nowhere near complete and all the big twists are yet to happen. There's just something about it that makes me want more every time the new story segment ends. The colourful characters, the humorous dialogue; it's just all around very light-hearted and not too serious.
Amount of content currently: I got about 14 hours playing the story from start to finish, completing most of the side quests and doing all 4 dungeons. I had, however, already played through the dungeons so I knew exactly how to do the puzzles, and didn't spend as much time as a first-time-player would've spent doing them. Currently, if you do all the content in the game, collecting the hidden treasures and completing all the side quests, I think you could get around 25 hours. This number is obviously going to change when more content gets added (the game is around 2/3 done I think) but already, it is easily worth 20 bucks.
Also: as you can see I have over 80 hours of playtime on CrossCode which just goes to show that the game is so good I'm willing to play it multiple times from the beginning even though it has pretty much no replayability value as of yet (that will change when they add the NG+ mode).

I bought this game because I had to know if it was real. There was no way a game could judge art, right?
WRONG.
This game delivers on its promise: you get to make art, and your art gets judged, by a bevy of types of art buffs, who have varying tastes that yes, are noticeably different. Paintings appeal to various art buffs according to consistent rules...
...rules you will need to find out on your own, as that's basically the game.
The game doesn't provide you with much instruction and it shouldn't need to. There is not too much exposition or story, other than your story from the bottom to...well, that's up to you.
A lot of people don't seem to get this: there are multiple endings and multiple paths to the endings. I think the reason most people don't get this is because they draw according to what they wanna draw, over and over, so they end up with the same results, leading to the same paths and endings over and over. I recommend challenging yourself to paint differently each time to see how you can affect your outcome.
My spoiler free tips:
Take your time on paintings. I know it seems like a lot of people online are making paintings quickly and selling them for loads, but you don't see that the Let's Plays have cuts, and many LPers have some creative experience in a visual arts field.
Use whatever tools you want, but I recommend building "layers" slowly.
Learn to use oekaki painting techniques. Example, I know how to dither using the spray paint tool by going over the edges between colors with the spraypaint can to blend together the colors.
Do not look up spoilers or tips online regarding how to please customers, because those customer pleasing tips are spoilers for the entire game.
On replay, try, try, try to paint differently if you want to have a different kind of runthrough than the last one you had.

Loadout is a arena shooter that's basically what you get if you mix the unique character designs of Team Fortress 2, the gameplay of Call of Duty with a few more bells and whistles, some INSANE weapons, and give it three tons of cocaine.
You can play as one of three characters, a crack-head Commando, a stereotypical black guy, and a FAT lady, and you just shoot the hell out of each other.
Story? HA! There is none! You just shoot each other for the sake of shooting each other. For most games, like Call of Duty, this would get boring REALLY quick, but in this case, it makes things more fun, thanks to how insane the characters are, you can see some characters flip off the guy that killed him/her....while they're DEAD!
Speaking of which, you can actually see the damage you do with each weapon! You can blow off the legs, arms, and even turn your opponent's chest into swiss cheese! It has an incredible amount of detail in it, and I'm thankful for that.
As for the weapons, there isn't a default one.....because you MAKE THE WEAPONS! That's right, you, the player, make the guns you use! Ranging from a Sniper rifle that shoots lasers, to a spike ball launcher that shocks people.
Character customization is your usual "Want this? Give us # coins please" kind of thing, but thankfully you can earn the coins in the game by just playing it. You can get shirts, necklaces, taunts, that sort of thing.

This is an absolutely amazing game. It's the most recent installment in a series of great games, and it's very well done, especially for having been created by a small studio like GiaB.
The scope of this game is massive; each of the 191 fields can take you anywhere from 20 minutes to 3 hours, depending on if you just want to get it over with, or farm the hell out of it for experience and achievements.
The combat system is the best feature of this game, making it what is, Gemcraft. The ability to combine gems in any manner you choose gives you an insane amount of possibilities for how to build your defences, as well as having traps, towers, and amplifiers to place those gems in.
Every field is a different challenge that requires different strategies to beat, and with 191 of them, that's a lot of strategies you can use. (Ok, really there's about a dozen different strategies, but you can implement them in a lot of different ways).
This is by far the best 2D tower defence game I have ever played (or seen, for that matter) and I would personally rank it in the top 3 of all TD games. I doubt anyone else would fail to list it in the top 5, depending on their personal preferences.

The Binding of Isaac was definitely worth my time. The game was heavily intuitive at the beginning, and I could tell what any enemy was going to do just by looking at it, which allowed me to beat Mom on my third run despite having no real outside knowledge of the game (there was no excuse for losing the second run, but on the first run I came up against The Bloat. I mean, come on)!
Despite this, the game also offers a real challenge, especially with the Eternal edition. Trying to get the eternal achievement for every character sure isn't easy, but I'll do it at some point. Honestly.
The different characters also all have their strengths and weaknesses. For instance, Isaac's strength is that he's got well balanced stats (and the D6), but his weakness is that his stats sometimes feel a bit too balanced. Judas' strength is his offensive capabilities, which are immense, but he has next to no health. Eve's strength is her design, her weakness is her stats. You get the idea.
Different characters will be better for different players, but you can't just take your favourite and only roll with that, or else you can't get 100%. The game forces you to get better and better, adding much more to its replayability.
I'm very glad of this purchase, and I'm looking forward to playing the remake after I 100% this. I could honestly recommend it to anyone who likes video games.

If there was ever a first-person version of Dwarf Fortress, Wurm would be it. Wurm has challenging controls, incredible levels of complexity, and a very steep learning curve. I'm 40 hours of play in, and I'm still glued to the wiki learning learning how everything works. There are still a lot of sharp edges, even though other things are tremendously polished, and goodness will the interface try and fight you.
The game also provides an incredible amount of customisation. You can make your own keybindings for every action. You can build the tiniest hut to the largest castle. You can form alliances and go to war. And the fact that *everything* in the game is player made is stunning.
It's pleasing to see there have been recent updates pushed, so the game is continuing is grow and improve. It's also pleasing to see a lot of developer feedback in the forums towards player ideas and suggestions.
If you want a game to be immediately friendly and easy to use, wurm isn't what you're after. But if you have a lot of time to sink into a game, enjoy creative/sandbox games, and have existing friends playing, this is worth it. If you have those without friends, and the game is on special, then it's also worth it as you'll make friends on one of the many servers out there.
Also if you're using Linux, the game runs *flawlessly*.
A great game with huge depth if you're happy to climb the learning curve.

Okay so where should I start..
Let's start with the negative stuff cause that's usually what people look at anyway.
The game has a few flaws that I cannot get over:
-Depth Perception Issues. Not only is it often so, that you're being attacked by enemies that you cannot attack because you're not in the same depth, but it's also hard to tell which depth they're in at all, leading to some frustration from time to time. Also some items might sometimes drop in a depth that you cannot even reach.
-It's not hard. Now you might say this is very relative, but for me, these kinds of games is about growing in power, since you level and acquire new gear, so that you may overcome harder challenges. This point is especially important since your experience & gold is saved, even if you die, so you can just keep doing the same thing til' you get past it. Sure, you might die here there once or twice, but we beat every level in the first try and overall found the game to be too easy. Even on the last boss we made it without grinding a single level twice and we didn't even dodge most of his attacks.
-The game is very short. A little over 5 hours of gameplay was enough to beat the entire game with one class, and that's taking into account idling in the menu probably about 30 minutes and restarting it due to bugs like being unable to move or even just crashes.
-Tanky monsters. When I'm saying that I'm not talking about the bosses, the bosses are fine. But this is something I see very often in games. Instead of making the monsters challenging enough, you make them very tanky, so that it'll still take time to take them down. It's not fun, it's just repetitive and tedious.
-Constant knockback. You're constantly being knockbacked, there's really nothing to explain here, you'll spend at least about 30% of your time in combat lying on the ground.
Those are the main points for me that are bad. But here's the good ones.
-Story. It's definitely not that great of a story, but it's somewhat humorous and you want to find out what happens, so I have no complaints, the story did what it was supposed to do, it made me want to play on.
-Gear, I felt the excitement for getting a better weapon/armor. That's at least more than what many other games do.
-Pretty fun multiplayer. Since you're constantly getting knockbacked, mashing buttons, filling up the screen with you power attacks or getting thrown around and ending up in bad positions, it's pretty fun to play co-op in it. As always it's more fun to play with friends.
-Music. The music was not that kind of music that got stuck in your head or something you'll sing/dig along to, but it was decent, and I have no complaints about it either.
-Graphics. The graphic design is nice and overall I enjoyed going through the world, especially paying attention to the background scenery at times.
Overall I must say this is a pretty mediocre game from a game design perspective, but it was decent entertainment for the 5 hours I played it. Do I consider it to be worth 10 euros though? No.

For as long as I can remember, I have always loved Resident Evil. I remember my heli crashing and being locked in a church with dogs coming at me all the way back on the PS1. Rather it be movie or videogame based, the experience has always been enjoyable.
As for Revalations itself, the game and story was great.
Gameplay wise, everything felt smooth. Framerate was great, even when playing on my laptop. I could record with no issues at all, no lag or frame drop at all. The controls were set ideally for a PC gamer unlike Resident Evil 6 where you need to hit left control, shift, and S to do a roll. Looking more in depth, there was an ample amount of different weapons to use and an interesting "weapon mod system."
As always, Mercenaries makes a return and is actually pretty fun due to the new weapon system, the 20 or so characters you can pick from, the 50 maps, and once again how smooth it runs.
The story was good and fairly different from my experience even after Resident Evil 6. There were twists and turns and I did not expect anything that happened, it was a nice change in pace.
The only two complaints are:
1. Once I got into the story and how to play the game, I flew through the story in nearly 6 hours.
2. The opening of certain doors causes major frame drop.
The only thing I could ask for is some campaign extensions, or another game soon.

As a fan of Super Smash Bros, I found this rather addicting. However, there is quite a number of flaws.
Starting with the gameplay, I'm sure it would suit any serious gamer whether they played Smash Bros. or not. Comparing the game to Smash Bros. doesn't seem like a wise thing to do, but it's hard to resist for most. While this game is significantly more simple, it's probably for the best if you're playing with a keyboard. Gamepads aren't something everyone has, after all. In conclusion, the gameplay is excellent, despite how it had to be keyboard-friendly since a gamepad isn't something everyone like me owns.
Customization? In some cases, there's not quite much, but in other cases, there's plenty of it. There are different parts you can use as heads, arms, legs, etc. that give you special attacks, while other parts simply raise your stats such as damage, movement speed, armour, and attack speed. However, even though reskins can be acceptable, there are just a little too many bearing the same ability, such as the teleport. It's also really easy to use these abilities to take advantage of how dumb the AI is in some cases, making them considerably overpowered. You can use the sniper arm to repeatedly back an enemy into a wall, dealing quite some damage with each shot. You can also use the slice dash move to dash back and forth across an enemy, knocking them straight into the air and landing back down just in time for you to dash again. There are even a few cheap attacks the enemy can spam at you, the main offenders being the blaster or the drill, which are definitely noticable in the tournament.
While we're stepping into the gripes, I'll address my biggest; wasted potential. This game had a chance to become the perfect PC variation of Super Smash Bros, but its severe lack of content is a big glaring issue. The biggest, though; no online multiplayer? Now, I understand that this was made by only 2 people who claim to have no networking knowledge, but come on! A game like this just
online multiplayer!
So in conlusion, this game is
worth the price, but I would highly recommend it if you're looking for a fun time-waster that lasts a long time. In fact, it's possibly the best single-player time waster there is. Kind of awkward in some places, but still a great game.

Loadout is a melting pot, if you will, of ideas borrowed from other popular shooters, with its' own unique flair. These include the inherent silliness of Team Fortress 2, the fast pace and reliance on pickups from Quake, the tried-and-true gamem modes of Call of Duty, the weapon customization from Blacklight: Retrubution, and said weapons' payload ridiculousness from Borderlands. What this essentially boils down to is a very fun and addictive online team-based shooter, in which players can create some truly absurd weaponry (want a rocket launcher whose' projectiles stick to surfaces and release electric grenades when enemies pass by? You can make it). Online matchmaking is fast, firefights are intense, and premium currency is reserved exclusively for cosmetics and additional loadout slots (i.e. there are no pay-to-win ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s running around with overpowered rocket launchers that their parents payed for). The game does have a few shortcomings, however, whic can essentially be boiled down to: (1) It is very difficult to find and join games that your friends on Steam are in, (2) The maps themselves often seem too small, even in Loadout's 4 v 4 games, leading to frequent spawn-killing, and (3) even though the weapon customization is the game's main selling feature, it feels like it needs some major modicifations (for example, non-default stocks generally only reduce weapon stats, and pulse-based weapons work very similarly to bullet-based weapons, yet have many more customization options available to them). Overall, though, this is worth looking into.

This game is the most gore-filled TPS I have ever played, and I'm saying that as a good thing. It is incredibly fun to play alone, or alongside up to 3 friends by using the in-game party feature. I am unsure if you can make a party of more than 4 people, but every match is 4v4 regardless of what you do.
It is hysterical and very much a "Dudebro humor" filled game, full of ridiculous costumes, taunts, and even the gamemodes themselves are really just filled to the brim with dark humor. When you die, your leg can fly off, you can lose your skull and run around with nothing but a brain and eyes for a head, you can explode into tiny bits, and you can give someone the finger post-mortem. That's just a few examples of death-scenes.
The free-to-play part of this game is hardly noticable, as the only things you can buy is cosmetics, taunts, and boosts to experience and "Blutes". Blutes is the currency used in upgrading your weapons, which you can only obtain through actually playing matches. Experience doesn't mean much, apart from rewarding you with extra blutes per level gained, and some avatars. It is extremely well-done, and I have not seen anyone actually complaining about it, other than the "I want to look like X, but I don't have the money." complaints, which is to be expected.
While I'm at it,
The key of this game, though, is the gun making. There is so many things you can stick onto your weapon, and make it function just like you want it to. A rocket launcher that shoots rebounding, time-triggered, fire mines? Doable. A shotgun that shoots healing bullets and has surface-rebounding bullets? Also doable. That sniper rifle that shoots electric projectiles that you really dreamed of making? Also doable. Of course, some things work out better than others, but that spooling trigger on your sniper rifle didn't really fit well in there either way, did it? Oh, and you can name a weapon what-ever your heart desires. Just don't name it something racistic, sexist, or otherwise offensive, as you will most likely be reported for it eventually. (Done by pressing F7, in case you need it.)
The gamemodes are what you would normally expect from an FPS game, and include;
Jackhammer - Capture the Flag, but you can use the Hammer to attack 5 times, and get bonus points for killing and delivering the hammer.
Blitz - Control Points, where you raise a pair of boxer shorts at a random place located around the map. Once captured, the next point swaps to a random flagpole location around the map.
Extraction - Gathering, except you can only have one "Gatherer" (Which you should try to kill very fast on the opposing side) per team, which can pick up the Blutonium crystals placed all over the map. The crystals can be used as  a grenade-like weapon, in case you need to defend yourself before getting to a drop-point.
Death Snatch - Kill Confirmed-like gamemode, where you basically kill someone and they drop a vial of Blutonium. Just like other FPS games, you can pick up dropped allied vials, and deny the enemy the kill.
Annihilation - A mix of everything combined, except for Extraction. Each team has a base, and your goal is to raise enough points for your team to be able to lower the enemy ship shields. Pretty straightforward once you get used to it.
There's a last option called "Custom Game", which is advertised as "Coming soon ;)".
All in all, I can safely say that I have had so much fun with this game in the just 17 hours I've played of it so far, and I predict that number will rise very fast in the near future.
I heavily recommend everyone remotely interested in a game like this to at the very least try it out. Since it's Free-To-Play, you don't really have any excuse not to, either way!
EDIT: I forgot to add that you can try out any weapon combination you want, before you buy it. The only requirement for testing something out is that you own it, or you have access to buying it for Blutes.

Α modern take on the classic formula of Panzer General, with added, meaninful mechanics (most notably supply and fuel limiting the range and time various units can spend on the map).
It is ideal as an introduction to wargaming, but also offers a decent challenge to experienced players. There are several campaign packs, covering theatres ranging from the pacific to norther europe (the Winter War DLC pack being a particular favorite of mine) and there are plans for even more campaign packs, so the game will continue to be supported for the foreseeable future.
It is not perfect, as the AI has the tendency, even on the hardest level, of making some questionable decisions, plus the decision to turn it "free to play" (a rather misleading description, as in its base form the game offers just 3 training scenarios and the initial scenario from each DLC) has angered people waiting for more substantial content within the base game, but neverthelles it is a solid wargame, approachable and offers scenarios which only hardcore (i.e. grognard) wargames have attempted to portray.
Overall, recommended and -even in its limited "free to play" form- well worth a try.

Let's first get a few things out of the way. The many bad reviews you see on here? They are probably justified, not because Nier Automata - the game is bad, but because Nier Automata - the PC Port is (quite notoriously) horrendous. The game still has not received a single update since release, yet Square Enix had the gall to push out DLC while ignoring every single complaint regarding the PC port. I was lucky enough not to run into issues, so I won't go into detail here, but be warned that this is by no means true for everyone.
Also, Square Enix took the♥♥♥♥♥♥when it came to the Asian region. The PC version was region locked and totally unavailable for several weeks for those in Asia, game wouldn't even show up in Steam searches. Then when they finally released it for Asia, they decided to jack the price up by about 30% (in my local currency) a few hours right after the release, which offset the benefits of Steam having regional stores and pricing. This was a complete♥♥♥♥♥♥move on their part, normally I wouldn't even bother with a game after seeing such ♥♥♥♥♥♥ practises, but the rampant positivity on PS4 reviews and my own interest in the game got to me. For once, I am glad I ignored my gut instinct.
This game is extremely good. So exceptional in fact that I am almost willing to forgive all the aforementioned issues. Final warning, there will be minor spoilers so don't read if you want to go in completely blind.
Probably the first thing people will notice about this game is the character designs. I will admit this is mostly up to personal taste, but to me the main cast (both male AND female) are some of the most jaw-droppingly beautiful characters ever brought to the medium. Besides the gorgeous designs, they have really realistic/detailed movements and animations, I pretty much never got tired of staring at them.
The visuals for the rest of the game are also absolutely stellar. The simple and dirty look of most things is fitting for a post-apocalyptic world, but that doesn't stop the game from throwing you painting like environments one after another. There is nothing much else to say here.
Probably Nier Automata's strongest point, which is an amazing feat given that everything else is already awesome. Almost all music tracks in this game are spectacular, easily matching the music of previous RPG greats like the Witcher 3 and Skyrim. Special mention goes towards the prologue theme "Alien Manifestation" and the Amusement Park theme, both I have put on repeat for hours on end while doing other things.
What elevates the music in this game to a level above most other games though, is their dynamic nature. Think another Platinum title, Metal Gear Rising (i.e. Rules of Nature), where the same track changes dynamically depending on the situation. This game takes it a step further than even MGR. Each track has multiple versions, some with strong/soft vocals, some with more instruments, some including the chorus, and even 8bit versions used when hacking. All of them are used in different situations, making the music seem to resonate with the current mood or context.
Other than music, voice acting in both Japaneses and English is also phenomenal, and effects all sound like they should. All in all, your ears will be in for a feast.
If I were to describe it using common genres, this game is a "semi open world action RPG". Environments are big and there is free roam to a certain extent, but not all areas are immediately open, with one of them changing really drastically as the game progresses. The game plays like you would expect from a Platinum title, really flashy combat ala MGR/Bayonetta/DMC, yet it has RPG elements due to the open world having myriads of quests, and a leveling system plus really indepth character customization.
Of course, this is not all the game offers, to list more of them, there is also:
All of this blends together to create an extremely enjoyable and constantly fresh experience, where the combat is tight and epic setpieces are abound like you would find in the Uncharted series. Yet there is no sense of "choking from a long, restrictive, and repetitive corridor" that you would usually get from that.
Thing's are not flawless however, one complaint I have is for one of the playable characters, who is limited in terms of direct combat but gets the ability to hack. Hacking is no doubt a well thought out experience, and as mentioned, it integrates into the story really well. Yet too much of something and it starts getting stale, which is what I felt towards the end.
The world that you explore also largely stays the same, and the initial "wow" for the various areas starts wearing off really fast as time goes on. The world itself isn't too big, yet still feels empty most of the time. I felt The Witcher 3 handled this aspect much better, but that's not to say what we have here is bad, just not the best it could be.
Another thing of note is the very clever and, for lack of a better word, "meta" nature of the game. This is hard to describe without spoling anything, but suffice to say the 4th wall here is thinner than most other games. To give some broad examples, the usual gameplay and interface elements (like death, or the UI) are addressed and sometimes directly messed with, and you are oftentimes able to do things that you wouldn't expect to be able to with predictably bad results.
Gameplay might not be the best thing ever, but it's certainly jam packed and a solid package overall.
I really wasn't expecting something this good to come out of a game of this nature. One thing first, if you do decide to buy the game, the first time you see the end credits roll and you think that's the end, don't be fooled, you've only played through a little over 1/3 of it. I'm not talking about some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t newgame+ here, im talking about fresh content and different/new perspectives with few repeats. You have to trust me and the thousands of others spouting the same message here, load that save file and start the game again, at least twice, you'll get what I mean.
Minor spoilers for the nature of the story to know what you're getting yourself into,
The tale being told is a gripping one, and the way the plot and overarching themes are handled is more intelligent than what you'd usually get from an action game. There is a lot to think about here in terms of philosophy, and the game doesn't just posture either, it doesn't shy away from addressing some really tough or uncomfortable issues in its own way. You might not agree with the game, but you can't deny an effort was made.
Its quite rare that a game manages to end well, a large majority of them start strong and fizzle out due to scheduling and budget issues, and you slog through just for closure. NOT the case here, this game just keeps getting better and better in both story AND gameplay. The true ending is literally the best in video game history, no exaggeration, you must experience it to get it.
Nier Automata alone is a 9.5/10 must buy, but due to the issues mentioned in the preface, it is understadable to abstain for technical reasons or even on priciple alone. The game is unfortunately going to be overshadowed by titles like Persona 5 and Zelda BoTW this year, especially because they released so close, but it is still easily my GOTY.
Please install the FAR mod if you do buy the game, it provides a lot of fixes that will improve the experience significantly.

I truly tried to get into Dispatcher. The game looks great! The sea monster creature looked scary the first couple times, but then like the game it grew old. At first it took me awhile to learn the controls and mechanics of the game. With the detailed character creator I had a nagging suspicion that I was missing something. Somehow I wasn't playing my engineer right. Quickly I learned that was not the case.
The game past it's character creator is entirely simple and poorly balanced. The fact I went engineer meant absolutely nothing to the game. You gain no special abilities, no access to tools others would be without, no entry into areas that a scientist or pilot would be denied.  It's just stats, and so you'd better make sure you make great choices because you'll never be able to level up in the game.
The game relies not on experience but a currency you pick up throughout the maps. No problem there except you must survive in order to carry over the money you've found to be able to level your character up. That runs into a major issue since survival is almost impossible once the monster sees you and it will see you.
Once spotted you must run, but there is no means of escape, no means to halt the creatures progress or to slow it down. It can follow you into duct and once it has you confirmed it will not let go. There is no way to lure the creature elsewhere when you enter its patrol area. Essentially the game is a chase simulator with no mechanics other than running.
As I said I tried to get into the game, but with no means of progression, the monster stale, the game gets incredibly boring. Perhaps it would be fun online, but no one plays the multiplayer. Although the multiplayer is a good way to give yourself multiple lives.
In the end the game could have improved itself in a number of ways. It could have included NPCs that the game seems more than capable of rendering in funny hunt, but are entirely missing in single player. Even as cannon fodder they'd provide a great distraction.  There are no abilities, the monster isn't hampered by in world hazards nor are you capable of exploiting them to your advantage. That's the theme with this game it feels as if there are all these features that can be added, that are meant to be there, but just aren't.
Not Recommended

Most reviews for this game are for the early access version, so I'm going to review the game as it is on full release. To start off, I have only played this game with a friend, so I am not sure how this game is to play solo. The first time I played, I found some batteries and then went adventuring down a hallway with my friend. Less than 30 seconds later we hear a loud screaming sound and then he hid in a toilet and I died. Basically, this game catches you off guard VERY easily and it is really terrifying when that happens. I think I've only ran into the monster once where I wasn't caught off guard, and it still scared the crap out of me because he was right around the corner.
Pros:
-A ton of fun to play with friends
-Pretty terrifying (a lot scarier than me and my friend expected)
-3 decently sizes maps to play on (all on the same ship, just different areas)
-FANTASTIC atmosphere (sound and graphical design)
-Beautiful graphics, on par with alien isolation and soma
-Bonus mode where you and your friends compete to see how many humans you can "infect"(kill). I am sort of indifferent about this mode, at least for now, as there aren't any options. If you could choose how long the game would last for, and you could customize how many humans there were, it would make it a lot better.
Cons:
-There are some cheap ways to die; i.e. mines on the ground, the green radiation that can infect and kill you(although this can be remedied by taking pills).
-Not really that much of a variation between all 3 maps (which can be a good thing, because it's all supposed to be on one ship anyways. It's also very easy to get lost, which in a horror game, depending on who you are, is a good/bad thing.)
-Once you get through all 3 maps, there's not much left you can do. (Then again, I have been playing for almost 2 hours and only beat one of the maps.)
Overall, this game has great potential, and for what it is right now, it's very good. My only hope is that the developer adds more options, and adds more maps/areas to explore, and maybe even new monsters.

AdVenture Capitalist is an incremental idle game. You invest, earn, reinvest, earn more, and eventually reset for a boost in earning % when you go through it again. Resetting is necessary to get every achievement in the game before the sun goes cold.
When I played this on mobile phones, I liked to call it "Spreadsheet: The Game," or "Autism: The Game." That's an honest summary.
To many people, this seems boring. To those people, I'd suggest peeking at a few games like this to see what the appeal is. It's basically a distillation of most game genres that have some form of upgrade system, such as obtaining better gear or gaining levels and powerful perks.
Personally, I like these types of games. They satisfy that reward center in the brain. It's a perfect example of the Skinner Box.

This is my review of Steel Ocean, if you want a short answer, this game is okay. Bare in mind this is made by Chinese people, I don't have a problem with Chinese devs but I will give you a heads up. You know what to expect.
Pros: -
The graphics look nice in ultra. But lower graphics looks like a pug's face.
It's difficult. You need real leading skillz to do some MLG no scope montages.
The music is nice. I would listen to it if I wanted to jump off a building. (It's actually good)
Submarines. Are they balanced? Not really. As in combat, they're weak. But, as a scout & base capturer, they are over powered.
Cons:-
First of all, in this game there is no such thing as battleships/battlecruisers/super battleships/fast battleships, but they are replaced with artilleryships. Who thought that was a great idea?! If real life battleships were like that, then how the fish did the HMS Hood/KMS Bismarck sunk?!
Second, the battleships' main bat.... I mean "main artillery" have the ranges of an archer from the bloody Paralympic Games. I get it, they made it like that for balance or what ever. But seriously, if real life battleships have ranges so short that you can play the whole of the Call of Duty series in one go, it would be ridiculous. Like imagine the battle between KMS Bismarck & HMS Hood would be like if they had short ranges. It would've been easier if they boarded the ships like pirates instead.
Third, the matchmaking......... Alright, I'll admit that this game's community is like F1 fans // Dead. But, oh boy the matchmaking is long. EVEN LONGER THAN THIS BLOODY REVIEW. Also the type of ship balancing per match is as stupid as Nazi Germany trying to invade Mother Russia. My first bloody game in this bloody game is bloody awful. My team was all tier 1 destroyers. But, the enemy had a bloody tier 2 battleship!!! I think you can play an entire game in WoWs while waiting for matchmaking in this game.
Fourth, the UI is ugly.. Like really ugly.
Fifth, there is only one server, that is from North America ONLY.
Sixth, submarines can capture the base while submerged. (EDIT: Submarine may not capture the base, but their range of getting spotted is stupid)
My Opinion of this game:-
Overall it's an okay game. If I had a choice between World of Warships or Steel Ocean, I would instantly pick World of Warships. In my honest opinion, Wargaming truely nailed WoWs. With the amazing sounds, graphics and gameplay. I would recommend you play Steel Ocean if you have no other good warship games. But if you know WoWs pick that instead.
But, other people's opinion will mean nothing if you truely like a game. So ignore these reviews and go try Steel Ocean for yourself. There's no shame in it. But if you don't like it, just uninstall it & play other games instead.
My Rating:-
7/10

Resident Evil: Revelations is a departure from where the main, numbered series has been going, and the game works and is a fun, scary blast despite a few disappointments.
The game takes place in between RE4 and RE5, but the storyline has nothing to do with the main series at all. Aside from a few characters (Jill, and Chris) and a few organizations mentioned (BSAA, Umbrella), everything is wholly original making this game a good standalone for those curious about the franchise. The story is all about spies, bio-terrorism, counter-terrorism, and attempts to go into some interesting psychology behind the villain's motivations but it falls a little flat. The story is told with that same goofy, almost-not-b-movie quality that has become the staple flavor for the series, and for a tale spanning countries with some really fun twists and turns that tone works surprisingly well. Couple that with the game's episodic chapters and it feels like you're watching a low-budget TV show from the 90s, and it's great.
The gameplay really isn't anything too different than the rest of the series. It has an over the shoulder, third person perspective, shooting certain points on enemies will weaken them and allow you to melee them to great effect (I still think that Chris's fists are more powerful than shotgun blasts). For the majority of the campaign you have an AI partner following you around, ala RE5, except this partner doesn't need your healing items or ammo and can't be controlled by another player, which is actually an improvement for this game. Despite it's similarities to 5, the game actually made me frightened, which only the first game (the Gamecube remake) managed to do. The atmosphere is very well set up, and one of the main locations in the game requires back tracking, but it's done so well you feel like you're running hopelessly in circles. The most frightening, and challenging, part of the game actually has you search for a dead comrade, only to find she has been resurrected as a disgusted squid-mutant-lady, and you then have to hunt her throughout the games main setting, which is a creepy, derelict boat that sways slowly beneath your feet. This moment is when the game really, truly shines as you never know when she's going to pop out and scream in a girlish voice, "found you!" Unfortunately the rest of the game is nowhere near as scary, but it is a lot more tense than any of the resident evil games after the REmake and RE0.
My disappointments in the game are minor, but still important. After defeating the squid-mutant-lady, non of the game's bosses are particularly challenging, but they are still fun to overcome. However the final boss made me so mad, because he requires almost no strategy to overcome, just a bit of quick timing, he has way too much health, and the fight just drags on. It was not fun for me, some people may enjoy it, but I didn't. Another complaint is that the game is a port from the Nintendo 3DS, which is actually quite amazing the 3DS could handle this game, but it shows. It's supposed to be an HD remake, and some textures are bumped up to a higher quality, but a lot aren't, and some of the level geometry gets blocky, and the "hidden" loading screens consist of doors with spinning wheels, you try to open the door, the wheel spins, and boom you go through. It sounds like a quick and easy way to get the game into small, bite sized chunks and remove loading screens, but I once had a door refuse to open for nearly five minutes (yes, I timed it) and ever since then I would groan when I realized my objective was on the other side of one of those blasted doors.
Overall, this game is really good. I had a ton of fun with it, and despite it's few shortcomings it really is a fun game, I would recommend to anyone who wants a scary Resident Evil, and I would recommend for people curious about the series.

This is a great combination of old-school resident evil style survival horror, and the new breed of resident evil third person action games. Though the new resi 4+ style action segments are spread out across the narrative and it's used as a tension breaker.
The graphics are great, despite it being a 3DS port. There isn't much inventory management, and the save system and health systems are simplified somewhat. Lots of autosaving and the only herbs you find are green. But overall definatly worth a play for anyone who is a fan of the genre.
The only negatives are the terrible AI for your companions. They follow you around for most of the game and are completely ineffectual in a fight. However you don't have to worry about them surviving either as enemies will generally just ignore them. I think they're just a plot contrivance more than anything, and once you realise that it stops being annoying that they don't cover you when you reload.
I would caution against pying the full £30 for this though, as the campaign only clocks in at about seven to eight hours. Which may be  bit pricey for some people. There is raid mode and new game+, both of which I didn't try. So that may change your mind on that one.

While in GCL you were 95% of the endgame afk and waited for the remaining ~1100 waves (of 1337) to destroy, in GCCS you have to stay vigilant till the last of the 999 waves. Even with a good Wizard Level you will have a hard time destroying the last 10 waves on harder dificulty. This is because the HP and armor isn't capped compared to GCL. At some point of the game you have all data presented you in exponential style.
Some here say that you need to grind older levels to progress, that is definitly not true. In my current game I've redone only about 10 lvls so far. To get more exp out the levels I cramp up the difficulty for new levels too, that way I don't need to redo them over and over again to get to the end.
The gem crafting is more indepth as it looks on the first glance. When you reach a certain point in the game, gems combined in a special way are stronger than just normal 'u'pped gems. There are several guides and even a gem combining tool to help out with the crafting.
While there is a free version in the Internet, it is limited in some aspects (less skills, no endless mode, etc). The Steam version is fully unlocked, has higher resoultion textures, a few additional levels and it doesn't need the Flashplayer to work.
other features:
* Story
* Skills and upgrades for skills
* Talisman (like upgrades for armor and weapons in RPG)
* countless maps to beat
* 3 difficulties that you can adjust in different ways to make it even harder and get more exp (adjustable per map) + Iron Wizard mode (like a NewGame+)
Tower defense game at it's finest. Loads of levels, replayability. Not 'Only 1 strategy to beat all'. So many achievements. Hours of fun. Must recommend

The latest in a line of tower defense / upgrade games.  Previous games in the series were free flash games -- one of which has an option to register your copy for $5, to get some XP and unlock a few skills.  Which I did twice, on different websites, without hesitation.  To see if you'll like this game, google Gemcraft Labyrinth and try five or eight levels.
Cons; this installment has a short but noticeable loading screen before every level.  Also, if it's anything like the others, it will also have an exponential difficulty curve, making the later levels hard as hell.
Pros, games in this series have tons and tons of levels, and can take weeks to months to beat into submission.  It has all of the user interface improvements that the series has gradually been accumulating (keyboard shortcuts particularly), plus a few new little tweaks here and there.  There are also enough tiny little tricks to learn, that skill and practice do seem to help, though not as much as strategy.  There is also an endless version of each level, letting you hypothetically keep leveling up forever.
[edit] Fifty-some gameplay hours later, the above holds true.  Previous entries in the series had a difficulty curve that periodically jerked upwards, providing these little areas where you could get stuck if you hadn't leveled up enough (especially near bosses).  This game has those moments too, but they're much less steep and much further apart -- meaning you can go back, replay the first 5 levels with your new skills and powers, and come out of it with enough levels and XP to get past the part you were struggling with.  A+.
[edit 2] Two hundred hours in.  There are achievements for gaining levels, the highest one is for level 200.  I'm in the mid 800's now.  I think I overleveled.  Some levels are still hard.  I accidentally won yesterday, but I'm not done collecting all of the things.  Going for 100%, only 50-some achievements left to go.  At no point during this game have I felt stuck anywhere, I've always had things to do to prepare for the challenges ahead.  Send help.

Mana = money, with it you craft gem types to place in towers for different effects (chain damage, slowing, armor break, and a lot of effects not normally seen in tower defense actually). Megabyte Punch is a sidescrolling beat-em-up game where you can attach the parts of fallen enemies to your character to gain new combat abilites.
Graphics are great, music is great, and gameplay is tight and responsive.  Some of the level design is a little obfuscated and makes exploring every nook and cranny pretty time-consuming, but the environments all have their own subtle style, and scripted battles are paced nicely throughout.
If you're ever played Nintendo's Super Smash Bros. games, you will feel immediately at home with the gamepaly.  The more damage enemies have, the farther and faster they fly when struck. When they hit something hard enough, they explode, at which point you can grab their parts and attach them to your own fighter.
It's extremely tight and fun to play, and the local multiplayer is awesome.   You can play co-operatively through the story mode, or brawl in Super Smash Bros style arenas, where falling off is the only way to die.  Obviously online play would be a nice bonus, but sadly it isn't supported.
Highly recommended.
