THE GOOD:
- The main setting of this game, the ex-luxury liner Queen Zenobia is genuinely creepy, but also a lot of fun to explore. Fans of the RE1 mansion will feel right at home here.
- The monsters look horrifying and are tougher than your avarage zombie, and even though the game gives you plenty of guns and gun mods, you never stop dreading having to fight these nasty mutants because of that.
- As mentioned above, the game features a gun mod system, allowing you to customize your arms. These upgrades can range from simple stuff like "more damage" and "bigger magazines" to more playstyle-influencing stuff like a damage boost if you're very close to the enemy or a charged shot. This system is also available in Raid Mode, the new multiplayer variant of the game, where guns and mods are then available as loot for completing missions.
- The game also does a really good job of introducing new characters to the Resident Evil universe which really needed new blood to enter the stage
THE MEH:
- There aren't really any "revelations" about the RE universes overall plot, all of the mystery of the game is pretty self-contained - so if you're looking to buy this game for a new perspective on the other RE games, sorry. But on the other hand, this also makes this game accessible for newcomers of the franchise.
- Raid Mode is a very love-it-or-hate-it multiplayer variant, replacing the more arcadey Mercenaries. Instead of being a Horde Mode, Raid Mode instead wants you to follow objectives and get to the end of a stage, and all of them are inspired by the Campagin. It doesn't really feature as much replayability (safe for getting more guns and parts), but it does come with character customization and a meta progression system instead. You probably will need to find out if that's your thing yourself
- While the Queen Zenobia is a very good setting for the game, the game also features chapters outside of it that straight up play more like the actiony modern RE games where you control a specific character with a specific weapon loadout, and while they don't play bad by any means, they don't have the creepy atmosphere of the Zenobia.
THE UGLY:
- Revelations' handheld origins shine through in some places. The dodge mechanic is wonky, character shadows are pixely and the enemy AI is simple at times.
BOTTOM LINE:
Resident Evil: Revelations is a good game that is able to marry the old RE creepiness and exploration with the modern RE combat.

I own and have played every TW title from Medieval I to Warhammer. Of all these, although I do enjoy them all and play them frequently (except for Medieval I which frankly is too archaic and I can no longer stomach), my favorite is still Medieval II. Although the graphics are of course a bit outdated and it lacks some features we have come to take for granted in later games, such as tech trees, it still can be considered mainstream. You don't feel it to be that different from more modern TW games, which cannot be said about Rome I or Medieval I. On the other hand, Med II has some features that sometimes are missing in later games, such as family lines and royal marriages. Mods such as Stainless Steel further help to keep the game enjoyable and actual. Finally, it is the only TW game covering the Middle Ages period, which for many of us is paradigmatic for the type of warfare depicted in these games.
Overall I give it 4 stars; 5 stars if you dismiss the graphics factor.

Something I don't really have, which is why I ended up specialising in the minimalist style.
Another thing is that you need to make a certain amount each week to ensure that you have enough for rent and to also feed your addiction to wine and baguettes.
Initially, you have a brush and the standard colours with shades of each, as you progress you unlock a spray can and pen to further improve your artistic visions. However, more tools and the ability to mix colours or fill in blank spaces would be nice but given the asking price for the game, this is still worth it.
The game is split into three chapters, the first chapter takes place in a crime ridden alley with you living and plying your trade out of a garage. A neat twist however, is that depending on what style you focus on and which client you cater to, you can end up in what looks to be a half-built gallery (minimalist) or a nice cozy apartment/gallery (expressionist). For the third and final chapter, the minimalist branch will end up in a gallery and expressionist will place you in what I assume to be a countess's mansion as a private artist.
Of course, I ended up in the gallery because my minimalistic style was just too good for those snarky, expressionist loving ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. Clearly my masterpieces that consisted of a canvas coloured in two different colours was just too much for them.
Over the course of the game, potential clients will come and go, perusing your art and "critiquing" it, hinting at whether anything can be changed or not. This could range from a simple "this is crap" to "Good, but not the right colours". Then finally someone would come along and pick one of my disa... masterpieces, proclaiming it to be "a true work or art" and in some cases "after buying this, my heart may never be broken again".
What Passpartout made me realise is that I really, really wanted to punch anyone that criticised my work. Just like a true artist.
It took me just over 10 hours to finish Passpartout on the minimalist route and I like to think someday I'll come back to do an expressionist one, but that requires some modicum of artistic talent.
For a game that costs a mere £6.99 I got more hours out of it than most AAA games today, which says something. Some additions in the future such as the aforementioned tools and modes such as a sandbox or challenge mode would make this already great game even better.

The game is enjoyable, however the story is short, you can finish it in under 3 hours, and very repetitive. It also does not work correctly with my Surface Pro 3 pen, so I had to spend around an hour looking for a solution. When I finally found a way to get the pen to work, the game needed to load for a second before every brush strokes. By reading the other reviews I can tell that other people who use tablets also experienced issues. This does not deduct from my score of the game, though, because I believe it may be a problem with the tablet rather than with the game. Nevertheless, I wouldn't recommend the game to you, if you use tablet, unless you are willing to spend some time researching how to get it to work.
Onward to the gameplay. The game is repetitive and many paintings will either be loved or hated. The amount you are paid per painting also strongly depends on how long you spend on the picture; so even if you just have the game open on a blank canvas without doing anything for 10 minutes, it will still sell for more than a genuine piece. Also, customers (in the game) constantly said that the painting I made was a copy, even if I had never used the name or drawn that picture before, which was annoying.
A lot of the customers opinions are also predictable. Once I realized that all businessmen liked the same monotone, gradient paintings, I stopped painting anything else. This made the game very easy and less enjoyable.
In addition, like I said in the first paragraph, the game also lacks in a proper story. For a $10 game, I would hope to get about 10 hours of gaming. I even tried to get all endings in order to milk every last minute out of the game, but got bored quickly because of the extremely repetitive gameplay.
Just a note to people who want to hear the PROS of the game:
- good graphics (also different settings for better/worse computers)
- no crashing (although some reviews say otherwise)
- Ability to save paintings
TL;DR
All over, I believe that this game has a lot of potential but had not been optimized for drawing tablets, lacks a long or proper story, is too repetitive, and has predictable characters.
It is currently not worth the price, in my opinion, and would be more worthwhile for a price around $5.

A few things to note in terms of game play and PC port issues that I've read about before purchasing:
I seem to have won the Russian Roulette of PC port issues. The game has only crashed on me twice so far and both times was because I didn't save for too long. On that note, I don't have the unofficial patch installed. As for the screen revolution issue, I bought the game after the official patch (v1.01b) came out, so I didn't encounter the 720p issue. It's sizable and both full screen and windowed mode works well on my 1366 x 768 screen. (The only downside is you can't change the resolution. Only tab between full screen or windowed.) If I play it on windowed mode, I have to autohide my windows taskbar for it to fit. That's about it.
Some gameplay advise (with minor gameplay spoilers) starts here. If you're the kind who likes to do sidequests and get all the side achievements or like to explore, read on! Because I had to restart the whole game because of this issue.
There are a few short story-only chapters where you can run around the game area and accomplish tasks. However, the game doesn't tell you this. You can progress through the whole story without completing the side quests at all. But if you do like to do side quests, it's best that you find a good non-spoiler walkthrough that'll tell you when and where to do what. The game has a replay function but the downside to replaying a chapter is you CANNOT save at all during the replay; with the game's tendency without notice as well as the very specific conditions you need for side quests, it can be a huge bummer.
I found this out at chapter 4 and decided to restart the whole game so I can have the chance to save between side missions. That's about it from me so far. I love the game overall and I'm just very happy to get to play it on a platform I own.

My favorite naval game.
The main reason behind it is the submarines. Because this game has them, the gameplay is less awkard than other games. It heavily relies on teamplay, and it's much more important to keep a balanced fleet composition alive than going for pure damage or whatever. And because of that, you are much more interested into playing your role well. Sinking a submarine as a destroyer probably won't give you the MVP, but it will save the Battleships in your team, who will sink the enemy destroyers in return. Which will in the long run give you the victory.
So why am I talking about submarines ? Because they have torps, which are rather slow compared to shells, their main targets in this game are capital ships. So you are going to need destroyers (fast and agile ships) to sink them. Destroyers that are essential for scouting (spotting without being spotted). Light cruisers will easily sink destroyers, while Heavy Cruisers will beat Light Cruisers. Finally Battleships take the role of artillery, but they will need scouts to find targets. Aircraft carriers will bring scouts, torps bombers, dive bombers and airfighters to the battlefield. In the end, it gives to the game a much more realistic tone than World of Warships, with absurdities like airfighters on light cruisers (because WoW doesn't have scouts). It gives much more variety in gameplay.
Also, the game is quite fast paced, with games lasting around 15 mins, which is not necessarily bad, given that I am talking about a video game.
The skill ceiling is much higher, for the simple fact that players are given a lot of things to control. Players have to train and pick your crew among a decent number of commanders, which have their own fixed traits. All the weapons, at the exception of 13mm AA guns, are under the control of the player. It's possible to configurate the load-out of your ship (ammo and consumables mostly), like removing dive bombers from an aircraft carrier and taking more airfighters instead (I wish your destroyer or sub never meets my japanese ramming sub ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) ).
Some negative traits however: the graphisms are ok, but aren't up for 2017. The gold smoke is the only premium item that made me rage. It lasts twice as long as the default ones and you can take more of them. Ie you can take for 90 secs of smoke in your ships by default, but 5 mins with the golden smokes. And you will often meet them at higher tiers.
And no, it's not a copy of World of Warships.

I have played Panzer Corps quite a bit. This game is similiar in play but more challenging. I really enjoy this game more since you have to think a more carefully before moving units. It adds new, or improves on, tactical dimensions including: flanking and encirclement bonuses, unit suppresion, in and out of supply conditions, as well as concealment and entrenchment. Engineers can plant and remove minefields and blow up bridges. Keeping supply lines open and preventing flanking adds additional challenge. There is not a back or undo button, as far as I know, which makes you think carefully before moving your units. The scenarios provide unexpected bonuses for achievements. Scenarios have varied and multiple goals to keep gameplay interesting. Money to purchase or repair units is a bit too low for my taste, I've used the editor to add more money. This can be good since it forces you to make tough decsions like determining unit repair priorities. I would prefer an option that allows you to select different levels of earned income in between scenarios. There is not a file browser tab for file import on the editor. You have to copy files from the Program Files folder to the My Games folder, edit them, and then move the edited files back in to the Program Folder. Once the scenario objectives are met there are not any incentives to push forward and capture other cities. Even though they are not objectives they still should provide a reward. This could be money or even a surprise bonus: hidden gold, extra unit, new leader, etc. I have nearly completed Winter War. It did not provide Unit Specialisation, maybe I did somethehing wrong. The scenario 12 folder, 12_Viipurinlahti, does not contain the required text english, .png, and .scz files to play that scenario. Overall it is an awesome game! Order of Battle is a great game, a nice fresh look on games like Panzer Corps and Panzer General. If you like or love these games this one will give you a little bit modern look while honoring the old mechanics mostly.
- The game has a fresh supply system that gives you the chance to isolate enemy units in pockets without supply. These units cannot get reinforcements and loose a lot of fighting power.
- Experience looks a bit useless at the start but while playing some more I started to note that the extra stamina (not fighting power) that the experienced units have makes them less likely to retreat and they less easy loose there fighting power due to 'tiredness'
- In the free part of the game you can try the first scenario of all campaings. I read some comments that the game was not really free, well, luckily these great game designers charge money for the great contents. With the money they will eat, feed there family and make more great games. With the DLC options you can choose the campaigns you like. I my case I prefer the ground combat over sea battles so I won't have to pay for the campaigns I don't like, bravo for this solution.
- The graphics can be 3D or 2D (Panzer Corps like but more fluid and nicer). 3D is fun but I like the clear view of the 2D graphics.
- The scenarios are reasonable challenging (for me) on normal difficulty. It is fun to try to win but also finish all secondary objectives. These objectives give you nice extras, like a special unit, a commander or just more cash, which you need enough off.
-  In some campaigns you also get to choose a specialization after winning a scenario, nice touch. I read they will make the system even nicer, give you the option to spent specialization points in stead of having to choose a certain specialization (of two) at a certain moment, seems more flexible and even more fun.
All in all I played this game for more than 100 hours without even noticing that I played it much, that's a plus as well.
I focused on the Marines expansion first, which is an Island hopping affair. Smaal islands filled with a lot of units sometimes. It can be a little frustrating, walking in a wall of units and bunkers with your brave marines, but it gives the right frustrating feeling. You want to pass these bunkers but it takes a long time, there are snipers everywhere, you loose your speed, get hamered.. it's like it should be. Second choice was the Winter War DLC, filled with Finnish sky troops. These scenarios are more open and they give you a lot of opportunities to catch teh Russians in small pockets and destroy these units, if you manouver well. Distinctly different from the Marines DLC.
I recomend this game very much, after 100 hours playtime I like it more than at the start. Now go play it! :-)

So, if you want this game, you'll pretty much have to download the 3rd party patch for the resolution bug. It's pretty despicable that a primarily cosmetic DLC was put out before a patch was developed. It doesn't really seem like they'll ever fix it for some reason.
Also "Anti-Aliasing" is MSAA, not standard AA. Do not set it to higher than 2x unless you have an absolutely killer video card. I left mine at 2x with a GTX 1070 and got between 55 and 60 fps pretty consistently (minus cutscenes, which play at 30 fps for some reason).
Despite that, I would still recommend it. It took me 35 hours to complete the main story components along with the majority of side-quests, so the amount of entertainment is pretty impressive. The storyline was a roller coaster of emotion with no mercy.
It is also worth noting that the music is phenominal. It was not an after-thought or secondary element like most games. The music is dynamic and deepens the awe and emotions of the story elements and world locations. It's also probably the only game I've played that actually had lyrics in it (sometimes). Most were in "chaos language", which I actually found quite nice.
Make sure you finish endings A-E... you haven't really beaten the game until you do so.
Ultimately, I'm recommending it because I do not regret my purchase. If they just fixed the resolution bug, the reviews probably wouldn't be so conflicted.

For the 2 hours I have played this game (in sandbox mode) I, overall, enjoyed the game even though it is very simple but there is so much potential. What we have to keep in mind is that it is still a very early access game.
The building aspect is very similar to that of Prison Architect, which I am a HUGE fan of, so if you have played that game or something similar to it then you know the controls already but there are a few differences which seem to be the same as SimAirport.
There are not a lot of choices when it comes to wall and floor colours e.g. I really hate that there is only one type of wood and carpet flooring so I hope we get more colours to really make each room stand out.

Playing is simple, maybe too simple at the moment as there really is no challenge or "End Goal". Your students and teachers go about their school day, learning, teaching, eating and leaving...thats it. It would be nice in future updates if we can create our own schedules for each year group and see different types of students like bullies, geeks, jocks, cheerleaders ect. to make the game a little more lively maybe even problems like a fire broke out in the kitchen or frogs ecsaped from the labs (if we ever get rooms like that).
There is so much that can be added to this game like...buying more land to expand on, doing PE instead of being stuck in the class room, making our own scheduels , clubs, school trips. I will leave my list there as there are many many things I would love to see added in future updates.
Does the price reflect the game? No. I think the £14.99 I paid for this game is too much for the little amount of gameplay I get. So my advice to others is that it might be an idea to wait for it to be on sale or more things have been added. If it was lower say...£8.99 - £10.00 then it would be about right for what you get ingame.
It would be nice to see the Developers push to get more updates out in a month or have one BIG update at the end of the month like some games I have played, unless it is a bad bug or crashes which they update as soon as they have fixes.
Do I recommend this game? Yes mostly but a little no. Yes because I can see some really great protential in this game and as long as you understand that this is a very early access game and are happy with basic objects, game play and are also happy to wait for updates then go for it! No mainly because of the price, for me it is just a little to much for the little you get if it was lower then it would be yes all the way.
Overall score...6/10

The main problem with the game is that it had to live up to Borerlands 2, and unfortunately it didn't.
To put it simply.
Positives;
+ It's fun
+ Last half of the story is very good
+ New fighting mechanics such as using the OZ kits
+ Bad loot isnt obsolete with the grinder
+ Character actually has personality and belongs in the campaign
+ Cryo element and laser weapons
+ You can feel the characters changing as the story develops
+ Final Boss has new and interesting mechanics
+ Great ending setting up for B3
Negatives;
- Alot of the missions early on are the same, you go to a place to try and find something, turns out you cant get it that way, have to find another way to get there (can happen up to 3 times), kill a weak bandit boss and get poor loot
- Bugs, the new jumping mechanic means that enemies get stuck in walls even on flat ground
- Needless running to areas
- Fairly short story and not alot of side missions (35-40% of what B2 had to offer)
- Alot of enemies use DOT weapons meaing you die after you cleared out an area with no way to get back up
- DLC characters seem to be alot more powerful
- Some of the mini bosses seem like reskinned versions of B2 bosses (BNK3R is pretty much in the game)
Overall the game is enjoyable but I can only reccomend it to people who have played the earlier games in the franchise.
If you are looking to play a game get Borderlands 2 as it has more value of enjoyment attached to it.
Borderlands 2 > Pre Sequel > Borderlands

This game is like Borderlands 2's weird uncle. You know the one.
The storyline obviously wasn't deep in any previous game but it was always amusing. This game seemed like they kind of just went in one direction with it and never thought to add anything else.
The gameplay is almost cut and paste of borderlands 2. It does add a few new features but I would say that most of them are novelties at best and the rest are annoying depending on who you are. The O2 thing would be great...if it wasn't just another hassel to keep track of to put hiccups in the action. The low gravity would be great...if it was used for more than just one or two missions and the rest of the time was a little bit of a hinderence.
The only thing I like is some of the new and/or rebuilt classes. Then again, I would have gladly paid 10 or 15 bucks for those as DLC in borderlands 2. In this game it just seems like the too sweet frosting on a fecal cake. The low gravity should have been a damn mod for borderlands 2 and not a main feature of this game as well as the new element/weapon types. Hell, I would have been happier paying 40 bucks just to have some of these features in borderland 2 rather than have to play a second tier game to have access to them.
I also have to point out something that hit me as odd. Every single character in this game is bi-sexual. I don't even care about what sex somebody finds interest in, even if it's both. But my god. Every...Single...One. At first I thought it was inclusive when they revealed one of the characters swung for both teams. Then the next character was revealed to swing both ways and I thought of it as a bit of a joke. After the third one I started to get tired of it. If it was a joke it wasn't funny and if it was trying to include a minority into the game it did that poorly too by making them all the same. I get the feeling they thought it was a joke and then just kept running with it.
In the end, only buy this game if you feel like you want the world of borderlands 2 to be lamer while you play a couple of new classes. Oh, and want to spend money on what I just mentioned.

This may seem like a stupid reason for a review, but I think it's a valid warning to anybody hoping to play this game. It's very well made in the sense of implementing weapons and features, but to customize your character, you have to pay ***Real World Money*** for some virtual coins that you can then use to buy things. This also leads to people who spend lots of money on not only their character visually, but also physically. It's great to see a really fun free to play game, (and I know many others have this problem) but it kills the atmosphere to know that with the game being called "Loadout". you have to pay if you want more than a few loadouts. In closing, I'm not saying this game is bad, or the devs are doing something wrong, but I am saying that I wouldn't reccomend this to the average free to play user, as it is a new style of controls, which can be hard to get used to, espescially with swarms of enemies that are armed to the teeth. Gemcraft - Chasing Shadows is easily the best online flash game I've ever played, with me investing 100+ hours into it.
In this game, towers can't do anything on their own; to be able to attack, a gem needs to be placed inside of it. There are nine basic gem types, each with its own unique effect. By combining two gems of the same tier, you will create a single stronger gem of the next tier. The different gem types can be combined, which will result in a gem with higher stats, but with less of each types' bonus effects.
This already is a significant innovation, but the game has plenty more new ideas up its sleeve: the combination of the traditional health and gold resources into a single mana resource, 25 skills to level up, special boss enemies, traps, collectible talisman fragments, three strike spells and three gem enhancement spells, and plenty more.
This is an easy recommendation to anyone who is a fan of tower defense games or strategy games.

First off, this is the most polished release I've seen in a LONG time. They worked on it forever, and it shows. This is, IMO, the game that defined the TD genre, and this latest release from Game in a Bottle doesn't dissapoint.
If you love TDs, this is a must have. If you like TDs, this is a must have. If you hate TDs, you should still probably try it. No, seriously, it's that good.

The Gemcraft series are something very close to my heart. It's not just a game to play. It's an art to look at in awe. A masterpiece to learn from. The embodiment of perfectionism when it comes to game design. That is Gemcraft. Never has any game captivated me so much, whilst being just a flash game with no budget and a single developer. Everyone should give the game a go. Just because the tower defense genre is saturated and full of horrible clones, doesn't mean that a few gems aren't present in it. Gemcraft is a game of planning, calculating, trial-error and design. Any player can learn a great deal from playing it about both game design and tower defense in all it's glory. Give the game a try, you won't regret it :)

Edit: Initially I gave a negative review, not because the game is bad (It is very good if you like Tower Defences), but because the game freeze. The developer contacted me, and found out what caused the problem, and fixed it, very fast and responsive, a highly positive experience!
BEST. TD. EVER.

I have played this game for about a year on Armor Games, so I am qualified to rate this, even if it says I've only played it 3 minutes here.  Here goes:
If you haven't played the Armor Games version, then this is definitely worth getting here.  Especially with the early Special Promotion offer.  If you've got the AG version, then it's totally up to you, as to whether you want to support the developer or not.  Either way, it is guranteed to give anyone who likes Tower Defense games many, many hours of gameplay.  Each level alone can give you 2 or 3 hours or more in a single Endurance run, and there are over a hundred different levels, starting with the 'F' hex, where 'F1' has 3 waves of a few monsters each, and they go up in difficulty from there.
Some changes I've noticed-- there is an extra save slot here on Steam.  Also, you don't start off with Orblets or with a Red gem.  It's odd playing the first few maps without 'battle traits,' but here you don't pick up your first one until F4.  Also, it's nice being able to play in full-screen mode.  And it's alway fun racking up Steam Achievements-- this game has 419 of them.  And in 'Chasing Shadows,' it's not pointless to rack up these achievements-- each one that you get gives you a free skill point to improve your abilities with.
The game isn't perfect, the way Gemcraft Labyrinth was, as Shrines aren't fun anymore: now they show up randomly, at random times and in random locations.  And I don't agree with the decision to tie the amount of times you anger a wave to the amount of beacons that appear-- in both cases I wish that I, the player, had more control over such decisions.  So some casual fans might find the game overly difficult at the start.
But for the fans, be it of Gemcraft or of Tower Defense games in general, these sort of decisions will only improve your gameplay as many of you now have a year of gameplay experience and already know when to use a white gem or when to use a black one, where to farm for mana and which maps are the best for early endurance runs.  I don't need to tell you guys anything as you already know and love the game.
So I'll add this one last point just for new players: don't be afraid to experiment.  There are plenty of guides out there if you get stuck, but sometimes it's fun to figure it out on your own.  Once you've played a few hours and want to optimize your gem ratios (and this can be as easy as deciding to make it out of two yellows, one red and one orange and four whites, or as hard as following the various high-level gem speccing guides which read like this: 2o+o+o+o+o+o+o+0(2o+b) + (2o+(o+r)+b+2b)+(2b+b+b+b+b+2b+(2o+b+2b) where r, b, and o stand for red,blue and orange gems. But you lose nothing by screwing around: even losing a level gives you shadow core, so if you want to try some prismatic gem to see what it does, go for it.  If you want to just keep playing F1 a dozen times before doing anything else, then do that.  It's your game, so have fun with it!

I've loved the style of the game ever since I saw a playthrough for it. Even being spoiled for the game, the quirky and weird storyline is wonderful. The insight into characters, the odd sidebar comments from the main character, the side quests, and more, were a sure-in for me in terms of whether I should buy this. I'm a sucker for the odd, dark, weird, and gortesque so your mileage may vary in terms of how you may enjoy the story.
A few things to note in terms of game play and PC port issues that I've read about before purchasing:
I seem to have won the Russian Roulette of PC port issues. The game has only crashed on me twice so far and both times was because I didn't save for too long. On that note, I don't have the unofficial patch installed. As for the screen revolution issue, I bought the game after the official patch (v1.01b) came out, so I didn't encounter the 720p issue. It's sizable and both full screen and windowed mode works well on my 1366 x 768 screen. (The only downside is you can't change the resolution. Only tab between full screen or windowed.) If I play it on windowed mode, I have to autohide my windows taskbar for it to fit. That's about it.
Some gameplay advise (with minor gameplay spoilers) starts here. If you're the kind who likes to do sidequests and get all the side achievements or like to explore, read on! Because I had to restart the whole game because of this issue.
There are a few short story-only chapters where you can run around the game area and accomplish tasks. However, the game doesn't tell you this. You can progress through the whole story without completing the side quests at all. But if you do like to do side quests, it's best that you find a good non-spoiler walkthrough that'll tell you when and where to do what. The game has a replay function but the downside to replaying a chapter is you CANNOT save at all during the replay; with the game's tendency without notice as well as the very specific conditions you need for side quests, it can be a huge bummer.
I found this out at chapter 4 and decided to restart the whole game so I can have the chance to save between side missions. That's about it from me so far. I love the game overall and I'm just very happy to get to play it on a platform I own.

As the developers have stated, they need a source of income and we should actually be glad that they didn't make the choice to implement microtransactions or some blatant moneygrab just so that you could play some other levels.
Personally, I was expecting something more of a mash-up between Hearts of Iron and Civilization V. I liked the looks of it, and I thought it was an interesting concept and since it was free I gave it a shot. Gameplay has a bit of Devil May Cry/Bayonetta actiony third-person fighting, with bullet hell elements, in an open world ARPG context. It's a unique mix that comes together really well. There's RPG levelling / loot / gear, but it's balanced well; there's no grinding, you always seem to end up at the right level to fight whatever the next story mission is. The game has Bayonetta-like dodging, but doesn't have the extensive list of moves and combo scoring; that would probably be overwhelming in this game, given everything else that's going on.
The game may be
for the timing or bullet hell-impaired. It does have Normal and Easy mode that go considerably easier on you, which ought to help, but Hard and Very Hard pull no punches. One misstep in Hard will
always kill you, and in Very Hard will
do so. If you've forgotten to save (there's no autosave!) you have to try to get to your body to recover it and all of your chips; failing that (dying again before recovery => body goes bye bye), you have to load your last save and do it all over again. The prologue is a potentially really brutal introduction, as it's a good maybe hour or two where you
and just game over if you die. The game reminds you repeatedly to save whenever you can, and it's advice you really have to heed.
The game is split into multiple 'routes', acting or appearing to act as a "New Game+" after the credits. There is recycled content, but these
just retreads with a couple lines of changed dialog. Unless you just didn't like the game to begin with, don't stop after the first credits roll!

Nier: Automata shares its predecessor's director/creator, producer, lead character designer, and composer, but otherwise it's from a different team (and studio) altogether. You'd get a couple throw-away references by playing that game that you wouldn't otherwise, but anything important is covered by exposition.

(Fix Automata Resolutions) to fix resolution issues and turn down the GI settings. I can run at 4k on my GTX 1080 and

No issues playing it in the office at lunch on a GTX 960 and a few years-old CPU either (drop a couple settings, use FAR, and it holds 60 FPS at 1080p). From what I've heard, AMD owners' mileage may vary though.

This game is a masterpiece. Yes, it's imperfect, and has defaults, but if it reaches you, it goes deep, and you're not likely to forget it. Ever. On that somewhat random chance, I recommand this game.
Now, let's talk about perfection and imperfection. Starting by imperfection, to act as a fair warning :
- the technical aspect of the game seems not quite on par with what's expected nowadays, and by that, I mean that many people have reported technical issues going from annoying to making the game unplayable. Myself, I stumbled unto two main problems : white screen of death when starting the game, solved by updating my graphic drivers, and a couple random crashes. So I guess I was lucky to get into the "just annoyed" gang.
- the game is not accessible. Many people state that it can be played whitout having played the first NIER, and while it is kinda true, the world's background is awesome, and knowing at least the synopsis of the previous game increases the overall experience a LOT. In the same spirit, the game has no auto-save feature, but a hard and old savepoints system, that unlocks only after the first 45 minutes. Yes, it means that you have to sit and play 45 minutes non-stop before saving. The tutorial is minimal, and thus you can easily die during those 45 minutes before having the chance to learn how to control the game. However, this "questionnable" decision is in fact deeply rooted in the core design of the game. It's one clear exemple of "immersion over practicality". While I criticize it, I also encourage you to accept it and push through, as it is really worth it.
To sum it up : yes, this game will require some efforts from your side, perhaps more than what it should, and certainly not what we're accustomed to nowadays. Even so, it's worth it, because now I'll talk about maybe not perfection, but greatness.
- graphically, I always place art design and coherence above technical prowess. You can criticize the graphics all you want, but the art design is top-notch, and I'm not only talking about the fanservicy first look of the game, but about the quality of pretty much everything else, from character design to animations. The style is well-define and brings something special, an identity to the title.
- but that identity wouldn't be complete without the beautiful soundtrack, one of the best I've ever heard, one that will stick with you for a long time, akin to the legendary Ghost in the Shell theme, if you happen to know it. That's the kind of soundtrack you have here.
- after the look and the sound, we have the gameplay, and let me tell you that it's a stunning achievement. Nier Automata provides one of the most customizable experience I know, combined with thematic reflexions about the video game medium. Just that. Yes, you can over-level and make the game incredibly easy...but you can also just select a harder difficulty, and/or not use certain core interface element like showing your life bar. Platinium Games has a very good reputation for crafting action combat, and they do deliver here with a very satisfying amount of weapon and skills that you can combine in different playstyles, and just watching your character fight is a feast for the eyes. Now, just let me ramble a bit about people complaining about the difficulty,  at any point of the game. There is no difficulty achievement. With the amount of care this game has been made, it's not an oversight. It's just that you, the player, have to choose how you are playing. I'll admit, there is no in-game guide about it, it comes from tweaks you have to make. Will I go for all the side-quests? Will I farm the best items? Will I play in Very Hard? Only one answer : try it until you find your style, and if you're not happy, push through, and make your own rules. So rarely have you that amount of freedom over your experience.
- and finally, the story. While it may not be the best, the narration in itself is very well done, and is articulated around twists and revelations. And yes, it may seem artificial and even weak at times. But that's not even what's the most important about it. Because this story touches philosophy. Not the kind you find in books, but the kind you stumble on when you stop your everyday life to think a bit about your life and your place in the universe. Sure, there are references to known philosophers, but the philosophic and metaphysics thoughts and concepts presented are not dry and complex, they're intertwined in the narrative, making them much more accessible, and engaging. This, imho, is the biggest achievement of Nier Automata. It's showing that entertainment can be thought-provoking, that video games, and Games in general, ARE important, and have a rightful place alongside other forms of Arts, like literature or film-making.
So, yes, I genuinely think this is a masterpiece, and hope it will have a big impact on the gaming industry. Because there have already been incredible video games in the past, but never with that amount of self-awareness. This game is a weird case of fulfilled ambition without pretense, and one last time, I encourage you to look past the imperfections. Yes, it's worth it.

CrossCode is a wonderful experience.
I could really let this stand like this and stop, but I guess I'll have to explain first.
In CrossCode, you play as Lea, an amnesiac player of the popular MMORPG "CrossWorlds", a game that takes place in the real world (Thanks, science!). Since you'd obviously want your memories back, you'll have to play the actual game, too. And thus, Lea is thrown into CrossWorlds, with no memories, and no language to use to speak, since her speech module is broken. Well, at least at first.
Over the course of the, relatively simple, but engaging, story, you'll meet plenty of memorable characters - from edgelords, to tanks, from glass cannons, to helpful other players -, some of which may even join your party to help you during battle - even though in the current version, this feature is only available with one other player.
In order to regain your memories, you have to play CrossWorlds, and for that, you have to travel across the lands and gather all the elements and become the Avatar- scratch that, and figure out the mistery behind the ancients, an ancient (Duh.) civilization that lived on this planet long ago. The world of CrossWorlds is beauti- and colorful. You will see frozen mountains, deep jungles or ancient ruins. The variety of locations and enemies is certainly there.
Speaking of enemies - let's get to the gameplay. The gameplay is actually rather simple. Click close to Lea for a melee attack and far away from Lea for a ranged attack. Right-click let's you evade or guard, depending on the input. And holding the spacebar will unleash one of your powerful special attacks. The combat is fast, precise and fun, but also rather challenging, especially when it comes to the huge bosses inside the dungeons.
Besides the typical combat, you can also solve different puzzles. These range from simple button-pressing to block-moving or arranging a certain path so your projectile can hit the switch. The easy controls make these puzzles quite entertaining.
The soundtrack of CrossCode is simply beautiful. I don't think I have to say any more than that. It's just wonderful.
Overall, CrossCode is a small, simple, but very fun game. You can have fun for many hours with the current version. However, be aware that this is not the finished product - the story doesn't even go to the second dungeon, and many locations are still not done yet. But that what is there is polished and entertaining.
You definitely should give CrossCode a try.

This is an odd one.  I recommend this game to support it, but it's honestly not worth playing.  Not yet.
The foundation of a fun game really is there.  As are most of the basic rooms and functions.  But it's also about as early access as you can get.
You set up a school.  Classrooms, bathrooms, lunchroom, faculty, free time and that's basically it.
So long as your students are healthy and happy, they go from year to year with a minimum of fuss.  Sure there's a few strange bugs and the AI gets questionable, but it's never really enough to get in your way.
There's no fights, no drama, no dropouts, no sports, no prestige, no head-start, no parents, no politics, no cheating, no strikes, etc. etc. etc.  Play it for 2 hours and you've seen everything.
So why the thumbs up? Do you like Tower Defense Games? Well, then you are at the right spot! GemCraft - Chasing Shadows is one of the most brilliant TDG!
The story never fails to amaze me even though i have already played it as browser version.

Each wizard level grants several skill points which can be distributed into many different skills improving for example your  gem damage or reducing the charge time of your spells.
Moreover during the stages talisman fragments are dropped which award even more bonus stats!
Gemcraft has a distinctive achievment system with up to 419 achievments! They can also grant up to 3skill points giving you another goal to achieve!
The stages are beautiful and challenging designed. On every map you have to think of a strategy before starting the first wave. Will you use traps or towers? Maybe both? Is there a way to stretch the monsters way by building mazes? Which one the 9 different gems will you use?
If you get stuck just replay some stages at higher difficulty to get even bettter rewards!
Overall i highly recommend GemCraft - Chasing Shadows! It sums up an amazing story, difficult stages and awesome mechanics!

What can I say about Resident Evil: Revelations ?
I bought the game during the Steam summer sale 2014 for 9,99€ and believe me when I say that this game is worth every single Euro of it, especially if you are a fan of the older Resident Evil titles. I almost regret it that I did not bought it earlier.
I do not know how much I can actually write about the game without spoiling it at least a little bit so be aware of it. You have been warned.
Capcom tried to get back to the roots with this game after the more action based Resident Evil 5 and 6.
Therefore you will encounter a lot less of the "Call of Duty" feeling where you have to shoot your way through the levels. In addition to that there are no real quick time events either. However, there are some little passages within the game where you have to shoot your way through the monsters. Thankfully, these passages are rather short and do not ruin the game to much.
You play the game mainly as Jill Valentine who was sent out with her partner Parker Luciani to find Chris Redfield. Even though the main character is Jill you will have to play some different characters as well. The story might be confusing at first sight, because there are some jumps here and there, but it will all make sense in the end.
The biggest part of the game plays on a ship, which is huge by the way. During your progress you will unlock new rooms and areas of the ship and some of them are really pretty. You will need to backtrack a couple of times to get new keys etc. to open new areas so a good memory or good map reading skills are recommended otherwise you will run in circles =)
There are even some riddles in the game, but sadly they are not really worth mentioning. Oh I almost forgot about the "shock moments". Some of them really catched me off guard. I really recommend to play this game with lights out in the evening, preferably with a good headset.
I did my first playthrough on the normal difficulty and in comparison to Resident Evil 5 and 6 I actually managed to run out of ammo sometimes so do not waste you bullets. I can only imagine how brutal the hardest difficulty must be which I will definitely try to beat. By the way the last boss of the game really deserves to be called "boss". Personaly, I think it was one of the most hardest bossfights in my Resident Evil history. Maybe because I did not upgrade my weapons or did not use a rocket launcher (easy mode). Believe me you will be so much satisfied after you beat him words just cannot describe it. Dark Souls is a piece of cake in comparison, really it is.
I needed 12h more or less for my first playthrough, but I was really trying to look at every corner and soak up the atmosphere of the game. I guess you can finish it in 8-9h if you rush through it.
I do not know what else to say.
Buy it, play it, love it.

While it's not my favourite of the Total War games (that honour goes to the first ROME: Total War, mainly due to the period in which it's set and, well, Romans!), Medieval II is a near perfect grand turn-based strategy game. It polishes the format established by its predecessors into a slick, easy to use and quite magnificent product. The graphics still stand up well now in 2017, while the gameplay is quite superb. A few niggling irritations such as the frequent "Path Blocked" issues during a long journey on a crusade don't really detract from the whole, while the religion angle is skilfully handled and well integrated. Catholic nations have to be careful to keep the Pope happy (a slight problem for, say, England - surrounded by other Catholic nations where attacking anybody is highly frowned on by the Papacy); Muslim ones have to be always on their guard in case of an incoming swarm of European Crusaders. Diplomacy is quite often ignored by the AI: allies can turn on you without so much as a moment's notice, and the tides of war are such that in the space of a few turns, you can go from swarming across the campaign map, to being driven back into your heartlands with nothing left but a few ragged half-trained armies.
And as if your neighbours aren't enough trouble, wait until the Mongol hordes begin to arrive...
Best Strategic game ever!!!!!

After 20 hours~ playing I can't say I would recommend Order of Battle.
I was really enthusiastic at start and the game was very enjoyable for the first few hours I tried it. The boot camp campaign, which comes for free with the game, was really entertaining to complete but it sadly gives a biased glimpse at what the actual campaigns ( that you have to buy everytime a new one comes out ) and the whole game actually are.
First, the game is riddled with bugs that have been reported by many users but were never fixed or keep coming back and break the gameplay. Here is a few that I experienced myself:
- Sometimes, especially in naval combat, I can't move some of my units because the game mistakenly thinks I already did.
- Frequently, I can't seem to be able to place my core units during the "placement phase" of a mission despite seemingly having enough supply points ( which are required to deploy units ) to do so.
- Sometimes, the appraisal of a combat outcome will be wrong. The preview of an outcome is displayed as numbers indicating roughly how many enemies the units of each side will manage to take out. Sometimes, even despite the preview indicates that an enemy will be defeated for sure following an engagement, the said enemy unit will just make it out alive with one "health point" left. I genuinely think this happens, if some conditions are met, as a poor way for the devs to balance the story mode.
- The game features a mechanic of "efficiency" for each unit. The more your units goes through a battle or has to walk accross difficult terrain, the less efficient it gets. The problem being that sometimes, for no reason, some of my unit's efficiency will drastically run down even though I'm engaging much weaker and much less efficient units. I also think this is a poor attempt at balancing the game.
- The musics are broken; often, when returning from a mission to desktop, the background music will keep on restarting every second.
And the list goes on and on. But it really clicked to me that I woudln't spend any more money on the game when I realised that the dev themselves genuiely broke the game. Upon the release of winter war, they decided to change the balance system to make the new campaign "more realistic". This had the direct effect of breaking all the previous campaign by making most situations unfair or some objectives irrelevant. Here are a few examples:
- Upon reviewing the balance system, the devs greatly reduced the artillery units ability to do any damage. Consequently, artillery units perform poorly on any unit, in any situation, and in addition to having a really poor range of movement ( you are unable to tow artillery units or move them in trucks... ).

- The anti air simply has no effect on most air units. Trying to build an effective ground to air defense will never be worth it as it will cost you too many supply points making you unable to deploy critical units.
To cut it on a last note, the game also runs poorly for no clear reason. On any mission, after playing a while, low framerate will occur. I couldn't find any clue as to why this happens, since changing the graphical settings won't have the slightest effect on my framerate and also because this happens as the AI is seemingly not running ( low framerate at player's turn as well ). The problem seems to be more recurrent on maps featuring lots of water. To anyone wondering, here is my specs:
Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4720 HQ CPU @ 2.60GHz 3.60GHz
16 Gb Ram DDR3L SDRAM ( 1600 MHz )
GTX Geforce 960M - 2 GB GDDR5 SDRAM
x64 windows 10
So the game obviously suffers optimization problems.
I would recommend the game if I felt like the problems the old campaigns are going through were going to be addressed but sadly I don't think this is going to be the case. This game is full of great design ideas and it could be one of the best turn based strategy game out there but it turns out to be a huge disappointment.

Oh, and I don't like the damage system.  Unlike in games like the Battalion series, a weaker unit is far more likely to do NO damage, making attacking with a weaker unit entirely pointless rather than a potentially worthy sacrifice.

Order of Battle: World War II is a free to play game, but has optional DLC campaigns that you can purchase for around 10 or 15 or 20 dollars, all totalling up to around $80 (at the time of this review, SEP/04/2016) not including tax. I do advise waiting for a sale if you want all the campaigns, but you can still enjoy about 3/4 hours of play time per campaign.
But, for the main game, it's more of a sort of tutorial with it's main scenario "Boot Camp", that will explain how the game plays and how things work. This will get you, perhaps an hour of gameplay if you're a quick player. With Boot Camp finished, you are able to select the currently released campaigns from the singleplayer menu. However, if you do not have a campaign, you can click the desired campaign and it will give you the option to either purchase the campaign, or try the first mission of the campaign.
Each of the missions will give you about half an hour's worth of gameplay if you're particularly quick, but the campaigns feature a little more then a dozen more missions to enjoy, with optional secondary objectives to complete that will affect future missions along with five levels of difficulty, all of which help increase overall replayability.
Should you purchase even ONE of the campaigns, you will be able to download community-made scenarios and multiplayer maps without further charge. But, again, it can only be accessed IF you purchase at least ONE campaign. It doesn't matter which one.
Now, with this being a Free game, I recommend giving it a try and seeing if you will like it. If it doesn't seem like a game for you, there's no money lost and you can uninstall it no problem.
I should mention that sometimes, when there's a lot of effects going on and a lot of units are on a map, it's possible for the game to have heavy frame drops and input lag. Not a major problem with turn based games, but it can lead to motion sickness with frame drops and skipping. Lowering the graphics and effects should help with this issue.

Passpartout is an abosolutely charming game, full of great music, simple yet compelling gameplay, and has a great "indie" feel to it. I love how this game breaks away from some stereotypical "Action" games, and replaces it with unique visuals, charming atmosphere, and all-around greatness. While difficult at times, Passpartout still pushes players to find the in-and-outs of its game, eventually taking different and interesting alternative paths throughout it. I consider this game impactful, and so much so, that I hope to see more from these amazing developers in the future. Now that we've addressed the "broad" awesomeness of Passpartout, let's dig deeper into some defined categories. First up:
Visuals play very important roles in games, ultimately effecting atmosphere, playability, and player interest. If graphics are lacking, the entire game crumbles. Players become disgusted by the horrific visuals, and the game eventually becomes difficult to play. Luckily, Passpartout is not faced with this issue. Passpartout's graphics are inviting and calming, ushering in an amazing atmosphere. Passpartout's visuals cause the game to feel antique and quaint, which makes for a unique yet enjoyable experience. Passpartout's visuals can also cause, because of the fact they are so special, a bit of uncertainty mixed along with worry. However, this simply adds to Passpartout's atmosphere, making the game better than ever! Ultimately, I reward these visuals a solid 9.5/10.
Gameplay is perhaps the most important part of a game, considering games are valued based on what you can do in them. However, a new category of gaming has arrisen quite recently. This certain category includes games that replace action with other compelling adjectives, such as: atmospheric, rich storyline, deep, and emotional. Passpartout definitely puts itself in this category. From Passpartout's rise to fame to his downfall to poverty, there are many different pathways that can be taken throughout the game, all that provoke interests, excitement, and other emotions. Passpartout definitely provides a good storyline as well, telling the story of a thriving artist as they attempt to please the crowd. Also, despite being a game where you are required to paint, there aren't the wide variety of tools, shades, or colors. Passpartout is much more of a game than an art program. Please note as well, the gameplay can be bland. There isn't a whole lot to do. Unlike new levels with better weapons and enemies, Passpartout simply prompts you to paint what people like. However, Passpartout compensates with its visuals, simplistic yet deep storyline, and cool feel. All in all, Passpartout's gameplay deserves a 9/10.
I mean sure, Passpartout may be a technically good game, but what about player interest? Will gamers enjoy this game, or quite after the first hour? Well, because of Passpartout's simple approach, and the freedom to paint whatever you want, gamers will be playing this for a while. Passpartout offers a nice balance of challenging yet simplistic, so players still feel accomplished when they sell a painting, but won't rage-quit at its difficulty. All in all, Passpartout's player interest factor gets a 10/10!
Now for the final question. Is Passpartout really worth your money, or are you being scammed? Well, while Passpartout is short, but there are multiple paths throughout it, and plenty of acheivements to keep you busy. This game is totally re-play-able, with different paths to take each time depending upon which crowd you please. Passpartout is worth at least 95% of its price.
All in all, Passpartout is amazing, from visuals, to storyline, to gameplay. Gamers will enjoy this for hours, and it is totally worth the money. 9.5/10-Me

For anyone unsure as to what this game is, it is a basketball game based upon the NBA, the National Basketball Association.  The game has several popular gamemodes including MyCareer, MyTeam, MyGM, MyLeague, and many more.  A lot of the game is centered around your created player that you made in the previously mentioned gamemode, MyCareer.  Your goal in that particular gamemode is basically exactly what you would expect, you begin by picking your College and then you move onto the NBA, where your goal is to work your way up to being a star.  Your player's skill is based upon a rating system and the highest your player can be is 99 overall.
Now onto the review, the game definitely has it's strong points including graphics and the appearance of the actual NBA players.  The developers at 2K did an amazing job making sure every player looks realistic.  I also thoroughly enjoy the little things in the game that are often overlooked such as, the in-game halftime and pregame shows.  They are very well done and are quite accurate to what actually happens during real NBA games.  While you are loading into a game, they also show episodes of their own show called 2KTV, these videos go behind the scenes of the making of the current NBA 2K title.  During the show they also do a few trivia questions that allow you to earn a little bit of free VC.
The gamemodes themselves are all different, for example MyGM is about you picking a team and being the General Manager and making team decisions including trades, free agency signings, contracts, etc.  Another example is MyTeam, in this gamemode you start off with a random team, and the goal is to build your team from basically nothing to something special.  All of the gamemodes are missing some little things that I believe will make the game a tiny bit easier.  For example, my friend and I play a lot of MyLeague Online, we play our regular season games against each other and then we move onto the playoffs, but we then have to individually sim the playoff games to get our teams to the NBA Finals so we can play in a fun best of 7 series.  A small feature I would like to see is: an option to auto-sim two teams into the finals rather than doing each game at a time or risking that your team won't be in the finals by choosing the "sim current round" option.
Overall, the game is a lot of fun to play with friends, however if you are by yourself you can have just as much fun by playing some of the single player gamemodes or by playing with random people online.  I give this game a solid 8/10.  I would say it's a good pickup, but at this point in time, I would just wait a few days and get NBA 2K18 that releases on September 19, 2017.

Gemcraft series is the ultimate Tower Defense experience for me, and "Chasing Shadows" is the best instalment so far.
At first glance it may work and look like a standard TD game - monsters enter the map in waves, walk to our base along predefined paths and we have to defend it by building towers and traps, as well as occasionally using some spells. However, not only Gemcraft does it superbly but it also offers depth and complexity you won't find in most TD games.
The most unique and fun feature of the game, in my opinion, is the wave angering. Player can spend some mana to make monster waves stronger (by increasing monster numbers and stats), which allows you to gain more mana and experience from killing the monsters... IF you can kill them that is. This one feature changes the gameplay from simple defense to the "how far can I push it" competition.
Another feature, which adds extra replayability value, is the ability to customize levels. It's pretty fun to return to some of early levels later in the game to see how much stronger you have become by beating the level with some extra difficulty settings. You can add more waves, make monsters stronger, faster, tougher or tweak some game rules to get a harder map with higher experience multiplayer.
Ah, the experience - player character can gain levels and unlock various skills and spells which will increase his efficiency in killing monster filth. There is no level cap, however some skills (not all) have a limit to which they can be improved. Add to it a wizard's talisman which can be socketed with talisman fragments gathered along your journey and you get quite a few ways of progressing, improving and specialising your character.
However, Gemcraft originally being a flash game, has some shortcomings. To many people graphics would be the biggest one. Despite it being pretty "clean", readable and fitting the game's darker theme, it's still 2D graphics in low resolution without all those fireworks that other games have nowadays. Personally I prefer it that way, but to each his own.
I have spent dozens of hours (flash version on ArmorGames, so obviously Steam won't show this time) with this game and can safely recommend it to other Tower Defense games fans. If you are unsure then you may try the free version of the game on ArmorGames to see if you like it. In any case be advised that GemCraft is not a game you can finish in a few hours. There are dozens of levels and some of the later ones can take as much as an hour to finish.

Now that I've spend some more time with the game, it's time to write an extended review.
Don't mistake this title for your standard tower defense game that is fun for a few hours and then you've seen every gameplay aspect. No, this game is quite on the contrary. The gameplay mechanics offer sheer endless possibilites.
There are 9 distinct gems, each one having a different special. These gems can be put in towers (mostly damage), traps (mostly special effect), and amplifiers (buff adjacent towers or traps). You can also combine gems of different types and upgrade them. Instead of placing gems in towers or traps you can also throw them directly on the monsters for massive damage or buff the next minion, receiving even more mana and experience when killing them. You can call waves early, decide to save your mana for some seconds to gain increased mana regeneration, build walls to control the movement path of the monsters. There are different spells to cast and objects on the map to interact with.
Am I done yet? No, I've hardly listed half of the gameplay elements. The rest is for you to discover in the game!
Pro:
- Gameplay mechanics
- Replayability
- Different play styles and tactics for levels
- Customize the level difficulty in different ways
- Hours and hours of fun (there is no real ending in this game, you can always level and improve some more)
- Dark, moody atmosphere and story. I liked it a lot.
Con:
- Graphics are for the most part not HD, especially the land tiles may seem rather blurry / rough.
- Complex game mechanics may be overwhelming for new players (but hey, is this really a con?)
- Game slows down when a lot of action is going on, even on high end pcs. There are a lot of options to improve performance in the menu though, including a setting to automatically reduce graphic settings temporarily when the framerate drops.
Conclusion:
This game is a must-buy for all tower defense fans, and even if you're new to the genre or don't like it in general, you should give it a try. You won't regret it!

'Of Orcs And Men' is a fantasy action role-playing game developed By Cyanide & Spiders which firstly places you inside the role of an elite Orc warrior known as Arkail, a member of the legendary legion named the Bloodjaws: a league of warriors feared throughout the whole continent. Humankind have forever waged war upon your people and the Goblin race, but your people have always stood strong against the opposition. However, they are now quickly descending in number and are in desperate need of help. Labelled the most experienced and skilled of your legion, you are appointed by your Commander to lead a single mission that could change the course of the entire war, furthermore enhancing the possibilty of your people's survival. The mission assigned to you is to kill The Emperor - the man responsible for the endless bloodshed of your people. This mission is of paramount importance. If Arkail were to fail his mission, the Greenskin race would slowly and surely ascend into history, allowing Humankind to emerge into the present, not only as the victors, but as the most dominant race to ever walk their world.
After reading the introduction, I am sure you are now familiar with the overall story within the game. After reading multiple reviews based on this game, I can definitly agree that the story within the game is quite short compared to other RPG's. This game only features five chapters and based on personal experience, I believe each chapter is around three hours long, though it depends whether you choose to rush or take your time. That is an overall of fifteen hours spent per playthrough. As you can see, this game doesn't take a lot of time to complete at all. However, although this sounds reasonable, due to the short timings on a game driven by a massive story, it makes me feel as if each level was rushed by the developers and I really feel this game could have been such a massive success if they included more chapters to enhance our playtime, furthermore allowing them to express the story in a much better way, therefore gaining more favourable responses and even more publicity. Also, the voiceovers behind most character's in-game voices are just dreadful. Despite having the main characters possessing professional voiceovers, the same cannot be said about the secondary characters within the game. The voiceovers on these characters (I hate to be negative, but it MUST be said) are honestly laughable. You will notice that almost every character belonging to Humankind have terrible voiceovers comparing to those of the Orcish race, and this really hurts! (Especially when you're a Fantasy Geek like me). This honestly deprived me from the immersion I normally feel from these types of games, BUT! There are some distinct positives! Yes, although the game is short, they have managed to express the story very well within the short timings they gave themselves. The story alone is captivating but I just wish they would've put a lot more effort into developing and finding professional voiceovers for the game itself.
I cannot really state my own personal opinion when it comes to the music within the game; I played the whole game without actually listening to any soundtrack whatsoever... Yes, you read correctly. I can only really state other people's opinions on this subject. Despite not having my personal opinion on the music, I have read mixed opinions about the various soundtracks within the game. I have read that the music can be sometimes very enticing yet sometimes quite dull. I personally believe it all falls down to your own personal liking; everyone has a different taste in music and if you do decide to purchase this game, then you will definitely find whether it's to your taste or not.
Honestly, I was really impressed with the cinematics! (I'M BEING POSITIVE FOR ONCE!!!) They were really well created and it really helped to entice me. I feel like they did a great job! This is definitely far from the weakest points within the game... HOWEVER (More negatives? Surely not!), when watching the characters talk, their mouths aren't in sync with what they're saying. It really led me astray from what they were actually saying. Thankfully, that is the only negative aspect of this category. (BACK ONTO THE POSITIVES!!!) The facial expressions each character makes intertwines really well with what they are feeling. Their actions within these cinematics also compliment their expressions very well. Overall, they did a great job, despite showing some flaws.
Firstly, before I begin talking about this, I understand this game was made just before the ending of 2012 so I will not be comparing this to the latest titles as of the beginning of 2018. For example, I will not be comparing it to games such as: 'Assassin's Creed: Origins' , 'COD: WW2' & Other titles like this. I hope you all understand on why I am doing this. I'd definitely say the graphics on this game is the strongest aspect; the textures are well presented and are very realistic, the detail on each character stands out perfectly amongst their facial and bodily characteristics and the atmosphere surrounding them is beautiful. For a game of it's time, it really stands out among the rest under this category.
Personally, I found that the controls were quite difficult to get the hang of at first; the beginning tutorial does a great job on explaining how the controls work, but I read that a large majority of people struggled with the control system, despite having read the tutorial. It is very difficult to master the control scheme but once you develop a grip on how the game is played, it still proves a challenge to even the most experienced player. I personally didn't have a MASSIVE problem concerning the controls but looking at other people's opinions, I have to label this as a low point for the game.
Aaah, the gameplay; one of the best aspects of this game. The gameplay is absoloutely perfect for anyone seeking a difficult and an extremely tactical playthrough! The combat animations are well performed, you have the freedom to make your own choices (Similar to 'Dragon Age: Origins'), you can approach various fights in many different ways... Honestly worth the purchase if you are a great tactician. There is a range of combat animations both Arkail & Styx can perform during combat, and they all suit their performer's playstyle very well. Although you can make decisions during your playthrough, they don't neccesarily have a great impact on the story at all, which is a massive shame. However, AT LEAST IT LETS YOU PLAY HOW YOU WANT TO PLAY!!! This is what I love about the game; you can control how each character reacts to certain situations... I LOVE the developers for allowing us to do that! Not only that, you can approach a fight however you choose to! Hate fighting full frontal? YOU CAN GO STEALTHY! Hate being stealthy? TAKE THEM ALL ON IN OPEN COMBAT! Either way, this game delivers a great playthrough.
I understand: this game has very noticeable flaws which honestly really deprive us from the enticement we deserve, but this game is definitely worth buying if you're a major fan of strategy and tactical games. The Story is very engaging, The Music is fairly praised, The Cinematics are enticing, The Graphics are GREAT when comparing to games of it's time, The Controls are fairly difficult to learn & The Gameplay is excellent, even more so if you're a fan of these types of games. Overall, I believe it is worth the purchase.

Of Orcs and Men is an action RPG, that allows you to control the massive elite Orc warrior Arkail, and the assassin goblin Styx. Finally, a game that deviates away from the tried and true Orcs are bad and need to be killed trope, Of Orcs and Men lets you play as both on your quest to kill the emperor and free Orc-kind from slavery.
Set in a medieval time, Orcs are a hunted race. Those not killed in battle are enslaved to work on the wall, a massive structure that divides the human nation from the Orcs lands, or sent to work in the mines, which is usually a death sentence. Goblins fair worse, as no-one knows where they have come from and since they can’t be trained they are usually purged on sight. I found the plot and setting to be very well done, and it was good that even though you are doing evil acts (there is a lot of murder in this game), the game presented them in such a way it doesn’t feel like evil- this age is worse than the dark ages, and only the smartest and strongest survive. It felt refreshing to play as “the bad guys” in a sense, as those around them are worse and I feel by the end of it your actions are justified. You control Arkail & Styx (at the same time) and murder and stomp your way across the human nation killing everything in your way. It’s also good to see that Arkail and Styx don’t get along (not until their personal quests and done near the end at least- as they know each other’s past), so it’s fun listening to them ♥♥♥♥♥ and snap at each other.
Gameplay wise it can get a little repetitive, usually sneaking around an area with Styx to assassinate as many enemies as you can, before going into a real-time mode of pounding whatever is left. Styx is good for kiting, killing un-armored enemies and archers, while Arkail is good for pounding anything into the ground. Both have two skill tree’s they can level up, and while on easier settings you can pick a few dud upgrades, on harder settings that will hurt you. Some of the fights are broken up where you only have one character to control, so your usual strategies fly out the window when this happens, and if your upgrades aren’t chosen wisely then you might find some fights nearly impossible to get through. The split in the upgrade tree right before the end was really good, and lets you choose which aspect of each character you want to focus on (either controlling Arkail’s rage or unleashing it and either Styx’s gaining magic or better assassination skills). I must say Arkail’s raging and going uncontrollable early in the game was frustrating, but by the end I loved it (just keep Styx away from him). Most of the missions are linear, though some offer a few different paths through them. There are plenty of side missions for extra items and XP, and believe me you want the XP for the endgame upgrades (they are that good).
While I found Styx, Arkail and a few of the other main characters were designed very well, the environment backgrounds looked a little dated/blurred, but I thought they were still good, and I found the voicework to be well done. The music just plays in the background, it’s nice but I didn’t find any music scores that really stood out from the rest. You will likely be focusing on Arkail and Styx bickering at each other.
If you are chasing 100% achievements then it entirely possible, but you might want one or two playthroughs to make sure you know which upgrades to pick.
